<a id="api-AccountAdminPort"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AccountAdminPort`

Host-authorized provider administration used by account membership operations.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth`, `@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth/account-memberships`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AccountAdminPort {
    read(identityId: string): Promise<ManagedIdentity>;
    write(identity: ManagedIdentity, metadata: Record<string, unknown>, field: AccountMetadataField): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | `Promise<ManagedIdentity>` | Yes | Reads the authoritative current provider identity, including both metadata fields. |
| `write` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Writes selected metadata while preserving unrelated identity fields. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

publishAccountMemberships.

### Public members

#### `read`

Reads the authoritative current provider identity, including both metadata fields.

Parameters:

- `identityId`: Provider identity ID.

Returns: Current identity snapshot used for lifecycle and hash checks.

### Errors and rejections

Provider errors propagate and retain any acquired durable lock.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AccountAdminPort } from "@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth";
export async function readAuthoritativeIdentity(admin: AccountAdminPort, identityId: string) {
  // The host supplies an authorized provider-admin connection.
  const identity = await admin.read(identityId);
  return { id: identity.id, state: identity.state };
}
```


#### `write`

Writes selected metadata while preserving unrelated identity fields.

Parameters:

- `identity`: Authoritative identity snapshot; publication supplies both changed metadata fields and requires the port to PUT both in one provider request.
- `metadata`: Complete replacement value for the selected metadata field.
- `field`: Selected destination field.

Returns: No value; resolves when the provider acknowledges the write, before independent readback verification.

### Errors and rejections

Provider failures propagate; the provider outcome may be uncertain and the durable lock must remain held.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AccountAdminPort } from "@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth";
export async function writeReviewedIdentityMetadata(
  admin: AccountAdminPort,
  currentIdentity: Parameters<AccountAdminPort["write"]>[0],
  reviewedMetadata: Parameters<AccountAdminPort["write"]>[1],
  reviewedField: Parameters<AccountAdminPort["write"]>[2],
) {
  // Host workflow acquires the mutation lock and checks the reviewed snapshot first.
  await admin.write(currentIdentity, reviewedMetadata, reviewedField);
  // Read back through admin.read before recording durable mutation completion.
}
```

<a id="api-AccountMutationStore"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AccountMutationStore`

Durable mutation lock and audit boundary for account metadata updates.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth`, `@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth/account-memberships`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AccountMutationStore {
    acquire(identityId: string, token: string, actor: string): Promise<void>;
    complete(identityId: string, token: string, actor: string, beforeHash: string, afterHash: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `acquire` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Acquires an exclusive durable mutation lock before provider reads/writes. |
| `complete` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Records verified completion and finalizes the durable lock/audit state. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Remarks

A failed or uncertain update retains its lock. The host must reconcile it rather than auto-expire or blindly retry.

### See also

applyAccountMembershipChange.

### Public members

#### `acquire`

Acquires an exclusive durable mutation lock before provider reads/writes.

Parameters:

- `identityId`: Provider identity being changed.
- `token`: Fresh mutation token generated for this attempt.
- `actor`: Nonblank authenticated operator identity.

Returns: No value; resolves only when the lock is held.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects conflicting or unavailable persistence; provider work will not start.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AccountMutationStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth";
export async function lockReviewedIdentity(
  store: AccountMutationStore, identityId: string, freshMutationToken: string, authenticatedActor: string,
) {
  await store.acquire(identityId, freshMutationToken, authenticatedActor);
  // Keep the token until verified completion; uncertain writes require reconciliation.
}
```


#### `complete`

Records verified completion and finalizes the durable lock/audit state.

Parameters:

- `identityId`: Changed provider identity.
- `token`: Token acquired for this attempt; enforce ownership in the host store.
- `actor`: Authenticated operator identity.
- `beforeHash`: Reviewed pre-change snapshot hash.
- `afterHash`: Hash read back and verified after the update.

Returns: No value; resolves when completion is durably recorded.

### Errors and rejections

Persistence errors propagate after the provider may already have changed.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AccountMutationStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth";
export async function finishVerifiedIdentityMutation(
  store: AccountMutationStore, identityId: string, ownedToken: string, authenticatedActor: string,
  reviewedBeforeHash: string, verifiedAfterHash: string,
) {
  // Call only after reading back and verifying the actual provider metadata update.
  await store.complete(identityId, ownedToken, authenticatedActor, reviewedBeforeHash, verifiedAfterHash);
}
```

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-AgentGraphEngine"></a>

## [CLASS] `AgentGraphEngine`

EAOS workflow runtime backed by the official LangGraph StateGraph.
EAOS remains responsible for authorization, approval bindings and side effects.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class AgentGraphEngine {
    constructor(checkpointerOrOptions?: BaseCheckpointSaver | AgentGraphEngineOptions, options?: AgentGraphEngineOptions);
    addNode(name: string, handler: GraphNodeHandler, options?: GraphNodeOptions): this;
    addSubgraph(name: string, subgraph: GraphSubgraph, options?: GraphSubgraphOptions): this;
    addEdge(from: string, to: string, options?: GraphEdgeOptions): this;
    addConditionalEdges(from: string, router: GraphRouter, destinations: string[], options?: GraphConditionalEdgeOptions): this;
    setEntryPoint(nodeName: string): this;
    getNextNode(fromNode: string): string | undefined;
    describe(): WorkflowGraphDescription;
    describeRuntime(state: AgentGraphState): WorkflowGraphRuntimeSnapshot;
    getVisualization(sessionId: string): Promise<WorkflowGraphVisualization>;
    getCheckpoint(sessionId: string): Promise<AgentGraphState | null>;
    runStep(initialState: AgentGraphState): Promise<AgentGraphState>;
    resumeAfterApproval(input: {
        sessionId: string;
        approvalId?: string;
        bindingHash?: string;
        approved: boolean;
        approverId: string;
        approverRole: string;
        comment?: string;
        authorizeResume?: AgentGraphEngineOptions['authorizeResume'];
    }): Promise<{
        resumed: boolean;
        state?: AgentGraphState;
        error?: string;
    }>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checkpointerOrOptions` | `BaseCheckpointSaver \| AgentGraphEngineOptions` | No | LangGraph saver or options; omission uses an independent MemorySaver. |
| `options` | `AgentGraphEngineOptions` | No | Additional options used only when the first argument is a saver; otherwise ignored. |

### Returns

`AgentGraphEngine`

### Remarks

The default MemorySaver is process-local/test storage. Production hosts must supply durable, tenant-scoped checkpoint persistence, verified initial identity, live resume authorization, and writer serialization. This class does not serialize concurrent calls for the same session or implement transactional side effects. Mutating topology invalidates the compiled graph; configure it before starting workflow sessions.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `addNode`

Registers or replaces a named handler and invalidates compiled topology.

Parameters:

- `name`: Nonblank node name; __eaos_approval__ is reserved. Names are retained without trimming.
- `handler`: Async callback receiving a cloned state and resolving partial state updates.
- `options`: Optional LangGraph retry policy and serializable display metadata.

Returns: This builder for chaining.

### Errors and rejections

For blank/reserved names; handler failures occur later during execution.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
graph.addNode("finish", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
```


#### `addSubgraph`

Mount a plugin-owned compiled LangGraph as one parent-graph node.
Input/output mapping is explicit so plugin state does not silently leak into
the EAOS state, while the nested graph still gets its own checkpoint thread.

Parameters:

- `name`: Parent node identifier, subject to addNode validation.
- `subgraph`: Compiled graph with invoke and optional state/resume capabilities.
- `options`: Input/output mapping and child-thread identity; defaults pass state/output through and use sessionId:name as thread ID.

Returns: This graph builder.

### Remarks

Child config uses checkpoint_ns=name. A mapped interrupt stores resume metadata in context; host mappings must preserve tenant boundaries and avoid leaking child state.

### Errors and rejections

If subgraph lacks invoke or the name is invalid. Execution propagates mapping/subgraph errors except recognized interrupts handled by mapInterrupted.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine, type GraphSubgraph } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
export function nested(subgraph: GraphSubgraph) {
  return new AgentGraphEngine().addSubgraph("start", subgraph, { mapOutput: output => ({ context: { child: output } }) });
}
```


#### `addEdge`

Adds a declared edge and its display metadata.

Parameters:

- `from`: Nonblank source node name.
- `to`: Nonblank destination node name.
- `options`: Optional serializable display metadata, cloned on insertion.

Returns: This graph builder.

### Remarks

Without conditional routing, execution follows only the first declared outgoing edge; describe may list additional declared edges.

### Errors and rejections

For blank endpoints or uncloneable display metadata. Missing node references can fail compilation later.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
graph.addNode("finish", async () => ({}));
graph.addEdge("start", "finish");
```


#### `addConditionalEdges`

Sets a source node's conditional router and complete allowed destination set.

Parameters:

- `from`: Nonblank source node name.
- `router`: Called synchronously after the node with a state clone; must return one declared destination.
- `destinations`: Nonempty list of nonblank destination names; duplicates are collapsed.
- `options`: Cloned optional edge metadata and destination labels.

Returns: This graph builder.

### Remarks

A pending approval overrides conditional routing and enters the approval node. This replaces an existing conditional route for from.

### Errors and rejections

For invalid source/destinations or uncloneable options; runtime routing rejects undeclared destinations and callback errors.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
graph.addNode("finish", async () => ({}));
graph.addConditionalEdges("start", () => "finish", ["finish"]);
```


#### `setEntryPoint`

Selects the registered node where future graph execution starts.

Parameters:

- `nodeName`: Nonblank node name; existence is checked on deferred compilation.

Returns: This builder after invalidating compiled topology.

### Errors and rejections

For a blank name; missing entry registration fails later on compilation.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
graph.setEntryPoint("start");
```


#### `getNextNode`

Reads the first statically declared outgoing edge without evaluating conditional routing.

Parameters:

- `fromNode`: Exact source node identifier.

Returns: First declared destination, or undefined when no static edge exists.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
console.log(graph.getNextNode("start")); // undefined
```


#### `describe`

Return a serializable graph description for UI/API/diagram consumers.
Handlers and router functions are intentionally omitted: this is metadata,
not a remotely executable workflow definition.

Returns: A structured clone of versioned node/edge display metadata in insertion order; may describe an incomplete graph before compilation.

### Errors and rejections

If retained metadata has become uncloneable.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
console.log(graph.describe().nodes.length); // 1
```


#### `describeRuntime`

Extracts runtime status and approval display metadata without history, context, or approval args.

Parameters:

- `state`: Authorized checkpoint state to summarize.

Returns: Status prioritized as waiting_approval, failed, completed, running, then idle, plus current node/revision and optional error/approval display details.

### Remarks

Reasons and errors remain visible; the host must control their content and authorize access to this overlay.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine, type AgentGraphState } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
export function overlay(state: AgentGraphState) {
  return new AgentGraphEngine().describeRuntime(state);
}
```


#### `getVisualization`

Reads a session checkpoint and combines its display overlay with the current static graph.

Parameters:

- `sessionId`: Authorized host session/thread identifier.

Returns: Graph description and runtime overlay when a checkpoint exists, or only graph metadata otherwise.

### Remarks

This method does not authenticate the caller or authorize session access.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects compilation, saver, or description failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
const visualization = await graph.getVisualization("example-session");
console.log(visualization.graph.nodes.length);
```


#### `getCheckpoint`

Reads the current saved state for one graph session.

Parameters:

- `sessionId`: Authorized LangGraph thread ID.

Returns: A structured clone of persisted state, or null when no session state exists.

### Remarks

The host authorizes tenant/session access; sessionId alone is not an authentication claim.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects deferred compilation, saver, or clone failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
console.log(await graph.getCheckpoint("example-session")); // null
```


#### `runStep`

Runs the graph until completion or a LangGraph approval interrupt.

Parameters:

- `initialState`: Verified host session/tenant/user state; a nonblank sessionId is required. Existing pendingApproval returns an immediate clone without invoking the graph.

Returns: Latest checkpoint state after execution, interrupted approval state, or the supplied initial state when no checkpoint is available.

### Remarks

This method runs multiple nodes, despite its name. The host must serialize writers and make retried handlers safe for side effects. It installs no timeout or cancellation itself.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid sessionId, compilation, handler/retry, saver, binding, or clone errors except recognized approval interrupts.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
const state = await graph.runStep({ sessionId: "example-session", tenantId: "example", userId: "example-user", currentStep: "start", history: [], isComplete: false });
console.log(state.isComplete); // true
```


#### `resumeAfterApproval`

Validates a pending approval binding and host authority before resuming its LangGraph thread.

Parameters:

- `input`: Session ID, verified approver ID/role, boolean decision, optional comment, optional expected approvalId/bindingHash, and optional live authorizer overriding constructor settings.

Returns: Resumed state on success, or resumed:false with an error for absent/mismatched approval, denied authorization, or normalized invocation failure. A denial decision completes the graph as rejected.

### Remarks

An approved decision requires a live authorizer returning exactly true; a supplied authorizer also checks rejection decisions. Host writer serialization is required: this method does not acquire an independent lock or compare-and-swap checkpoint revisions. Missing optional expected IDs skip those comparisons. Resume failures can follow side effects; no rollback or automatic retry occurs.

### Errors and rejections

Can reject saver/compilation errors, live authorizer rejection, or post-resume checkpoint failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
export async function decide(graph: AgentGraphEngine, input: Parameters<AgentGraphEngine["resumeAfterApproval"]>[0]) {
  // Authenticate the approver and supply live authorization before approving.
  return graph.resumeAfterApproval(input);
}
```


#### `resumeAfterApproval.resumed`

True when verification/resumption reaches a readable checkpoint, including a resumed rejection decision; false on normalized failures and not proof that no side effect occurred.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.state`

Graph state loaded after resumption when available; may represent completion, rejection or another pending interrupt rather than final workflow success.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.error`

Optional explanation for a missing/mismatched approval, denied authority, invocation failure or disappeared checkpoint; some saver/authorizer errors reject instead.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.sessionId`

LangGraph thread/session identity whose saved pending approval is loaded and resumed.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.approvalId`

Optional expected ticket identity; when truthy it must equal the saved pending ticket, while omission skips this comparison.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.bindingHash`

Optional expected request/contract binding hash; when truthy it must match the saved binding, while omission skips this comparison.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.approved`

Verified review decision; true requires live authorization returning exactly true, while false resumes the graph as rejected.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.approverId`

Nonblank host-verified reviewer identity supplied to the live authorizer and recorded in lastApproval.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.approverRole`

Nonblank host-verified reviewer role supplied to the live authorizer and recorded in lastApproval.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.comment`

Optional reviewer comment retained in the graph decision; the host owns content/privacy policy.


#### `resumeAfterApproval.input.authorizeResume`

Optional live reviewer-authority callback overriding the constructor authorizer for this resume attempt.

### Remarks

Uses AgentGraphEngineOptions.authorizeResume: receives a cloned checkpoint and reviewer/decision metadata, resolves exactly true to permit resumption, and may reject. Required from either source for approved=true; when supplied it also checks rejected decisions. Omission uses the constructor callback.

### See also

[AgentGraphEngineOptions.authorizeResume](#api-AgentGraphEngineOptions)



### Example

```typescript
import { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
const graph = new AgentGraphEngine();
graph.addNode("start", async () => ({ isComplete: true }));
console.log(graph.describe().entryNode); // "start"
```

<a id="api-AgentJobStore"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AgentJobStore`

Host durable queue boundary with atomic claims and lease-checked transitions.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AgentJobStore {
    claim(now: Date, limit: number, filter?: AgentJobClaimFilter): Promise<readonly AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>[]>;
    markCompleted(jobId: string, leaseToken: string, result: ServerAgentTaskResult, now: Date): Promise<void>;
    markWaitingApproval(jobId: string, leaseToken: string, result: ServerAgentTaskResult, now: Date): Promise<void>;
    markRetryable(jobId: string, leaseToken: string, error: string, failureCode: string | undefined, retryAt: Date, now: Date): Promise<void>;
    markFailed(jobId: string, leaseToken: string, error: string, failureCode: string | undefined, now: Date): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claim` | `Promise<readonly AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>[]>` | Yes | Claims due/recoverable jobs using durable transaction/lease exclusion. |
| `markCompleted` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Transitions the leased job to succeeded and persists its result. |
| `markWaitingApproval` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Transitions the leased job to waiting_approval and persists approval result data. |
| `markRetryable` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Releases the lease and schedules the job for a later attempt. |
| `markFailed` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Releases the lease and marks a terminal failed result. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createAtomicAgentJobStore for the canonical implementation.

### Public members

#### `claim`

Claims due/recoverable jobs using durable transaction/lease exclusion.

Parameters:

- `now`: Claim clock used for due and stale checks.
- `limit`: Maximum job count, validated by the implementation.
- `filter`: Optional dispatch/user/runner/route eligibility.

Returns: Leased jobs, or an empty array.

### Errors and rejections

Queue persistence or admission failures propagate.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AgentJobStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function claimHostJobs(
  store: AgentJobStore, eligibility: Parameters<AgentJobStore["claim"]>[2],
) {
  // Supply a store already scoped to verified tenant admission.
  return await store.claim(new Date(), 10, eligibility);
}
```


#### `markCompleted`

Transitions the leased job to succeeded and persists its result.

Parameters:

- `jobId`: Stored job ID.
- `leaseToken`: Current claim token; stale tokens must be rejected.
- `result`: Normalized task outcome to persist.
- `now`: Transition clock; the atomic implementation uses its configured clock instead.

Returns: No value; resolves after the durable transition.

### Errors and rejections

Lease/integrity/admission or persistence failures propagate.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AgentJobStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function completeClaimedJob(
  store: AgentJobStore, jobId: string, currentLeaseToken: string,
  verifiedResult: Parameters<AgentJobStore["markCompleted"]>[2],
) {
  await store.markCompleted(jobId, currentLeaseToken, verifiedResult, new Date());
  // Completion is durable under the host store contract; stale leases reject.
}
```


#### `markWaitingApproval`

Transitions the leased job to waiting_approval and persists approval result data.

Parameters:

- `jobId`: Stored job ID.
- `leaseToken`: Current claim token; stale tokens must be rejected.
- `result`: Normalized task outcome to persist.
- `now`: Transition clock; the atomic implementation uses its configured clock instead.

Returns: No value; resolves after the durable transition.

### Errors and rejections

Lease/integrity/admission or persistence failures propagate.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AgentJobStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function deferClaimedJobForReview(
  store: AgentJobStore, jobId: string, currentLeaseToken: string,
  approvalResult: Parameters<AgentJobStore["markWaitingApproval"]>[2],
) {
  await store.markWaitingApproval(jobId, currentLeaseToken, approvalResult, new Date());
  // This records pending review; it does not approve or execute the proposed action.
}
```


#### `markRetryable`

Releases the lease and schedules the job for a later attempt.

Parameters:

- `jobId`: Stored job ID.
- `leaseToken`: Current claim token; stale tokens must be rejected.
- `error`: Persisted failure description.
- `failureCode`: Optional stable runtime classification.
- `retryAt`: Earliest eligible next-claim timestamp.
- `now`: Transition clock; the atomic implementation uses its configured clock instead.

Returns: No value; resolves after the durable transition.

### Errors and rejections

Lease/integrity/admission or persistence failures propagate.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AgentJobStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function rescheduleClaimedJob(
  store: AgentJobStore, jobId: string, currentLeaseToken: string,
  sanitizedError: string, failureCode: string | undefined, reviewedRetryAt: Date,
) {
  // Reconcile any uncertain external effect before deciding a retry is safe.
  await store.markRetryable(
    jobId, currentLeaseToken, sanitizedError, failureCode, reviewedRetryAt, new Date(),
  );
}
```


#### `markFailed`

Releases the lease and marks a terminal failed result.

Parameters:

- `jobId`: Stored job ID.
- `leaseToken`: Current claim token; stale tokens must be rejected.
- `error`: Persisted failure description.
- `failureCode`: Optional stable runtime classification.
- `now`: Transition clock; the atomic implementation uses its configured clock instead.

Returns: No value; resolves after the durable transition.

### Errors and rejections

Lease/integrity/admission or persistence failures propagate.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AgentJobStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function failClaimedJob(
  store: AgentJobStore, jobId: string, currentLeaseToken: string,
  sanitizedError: string, failureCode: string | undefined,
) {
  await store.markFailed(jobId, currentLeaseToken, sanitizedError, failureCode, new Date());
  // The host persisted terminal failure; no automatic retry is requested.
}
```

<a id="api-appendAtomicAudit"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `appendAtomicAudit`

Append a hash-linked immutable audit event and CAS-update its head in the current transaction.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/audit`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function appendAtomicAudit(tx: AtomicSession, p: PluginPrincipal, operation: string, input: unknown, result: unknown, commandKey?: string | null): Promise<{
    hash: string;
    version: 1;
    tenantId: string;
    sequence: number;
    operation: string;
    actorId: string;
    at: string;
    inputHash: string;
    resultHash: string;
    commandKey: string | null;
    previousHash: string | null;
}>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Live atomic session shared with the domain command. |
| `p` | `PluginPrincipal` | Yes | Verified tenant/user principal. |
| `operation` | `string` | Yes | Trusted nonempty operation label of at most 240 characters. |
| `input` | `unknown` | Yes | Input whose JSON-normalized hash is recorded; payload bytes are not stored in the audit event. |
| `result` | `unknown` | Yes | Result whose JSON-normalized hash is recorded; undefined is normalized to null. |
| `commandKey` | `string \| null` | No | Optional command/ receipt key linking command input/result evidence; defaults to null. |

### Returns

`Promise<{     hash: string;     version: 1;     tenantId: string;     sequence: number;     operation: string;     actorId: string;     at: string;     inputHash: string;     resultHash: string;     commandKey: string \| null;     previousHash: string \| null; }>`

The appended version-1 event with sequence and integrity hash.

### Remarks

Requires the caller's existing transaction and current authorization. Hash continuity is not an external trust anchor; real business payloads remain outside audit events.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid principals/labels/receipt keys, corrupt head/previous event, sequence capacity or transaction failures.

### Example

```typescript
import { appendAtomicAudit } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data'
export function audit(tx: Parameters<typeof appendAtomicAudit>[0], p: Parameters<typeof appendAtomicAudit>[1], input: unknown, result: unknown) { return appendAtomicAudit(tx, p, 'example-operation', input, result) }
```

<a id="api-applyAccountMembershipChange"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `applyAccountMembershipChange`

Replaces membership fields under a durable lock and verifies provider readback before recording completion.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth`, `@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth/account-memberships`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function applyAccountMembershipChange(plan: MembershipMigrationPlan, actor: string, store: AccountMutationStore, admin: AccountAdminPort): Promise<void>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plan` | `MembershipMigrationPlan` | Yes | Reviewed target claims, metadata field, and expected pre-change field hash. |
| `actor` | `string` | Yes | Nonblank authenticated operator identity; authorization is host-owned. |
| `store` | `AccountMutationStore` | Yes | Durable exclusive lock and completion audit implementation. |
| `admin` | `AccountAdminPort` | Yes | Trusted provider read/write implementation. |

### Returns

`Promise<void>`

No value; resolves after verified provider update and durable completion. Unrelated metadata keys are retained and absent defaultTenantId is written as null.

### Remarks

A failed/uncertain mutation retains its durable lock. Reconcile; never auto-expire or blindly retry. This function does not roll back provider changes. Defaults to metadata_admin; explicitly selecting metadata_public exposes claims to the account holder.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid actor/metadata field/claims, stale or inactive identity, failed readback, or propagated lock/provider/completion errors.

### Example

```typescript
import { applyAccountMembershipChange, type MembershipMigrationPlan, type AccountMutationStore, type AccountAdminPort } from "@alneas/eaos-server/browser-auth/account-memberships";
export async function applyReviewedPlan(plan: MembershipMigrationPlan, actor: string, store: AccountMutationStore, admin: AccountAdminPort) {
  await applyAccountMembershipChange(plan, actor, store, admin);
}
```


<a id="api-ArtifactDeliveryService"></a>

## [CLASS] `ArtifactDeliveryService`

Coordinates durable approved publication/withdrawal jobs with channel ownership and resumable idempotent host effects.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/delivery`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class ArtifactDeliveryService {
    constructor(options: {
        repository: AtomicRepository;
        ports: DeliveryPorts;
        authorize(p: PluginPrincipal, operation: string, input: unknown, resource?: unknown): Promise<boolean>;
    });
    execute(p: PluginPrincipal, op: string, a: {
        jobId: string;
        revision?: number;
        commandId?: string;
    } & Partial<DeliveryRequest>): Promise<any>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     repository: AtomicRepository;     ports: DeliveryPorts;     authorize(p: PluginPrincipal, operation: string, input: unknown, resource?: unknown): Promise<boolean>; }` | Yes | Real atomic repository, idempotent host delivery ports and current operation/resource authorization; construction does not validate or execute those ports. |

### Returns

`ArtifactDeliveryService`

### Remarks

Requires a real atomic repository and host public-approval/build/channel/purge ports. Channel locks serialize unfinished jobs per tenant/repository. External build/activate/purge/cancel run outside database transactions; a failed reply can follow a completed external effect. Ports must deduplicate by stable jobId. Recovery requires proof that previous workers drained, never an elapsed lease alone.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `constructor.options.repository`

Real atomic delivery ledger used for jobs, channel ownership and enqueue command receipts.


#### `constructor.options.ports`

Host public-approval, artifact, channel, purge and recovery adapters with stable jobId idempotency.


#### `constructor.options.authorize`

Live operation/resource permission callback; exactly true admits, false denies; schema validation follows initial admission.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified current tenant/user principal.
- `operation`: Declared operation name.
- `input`: Operation input to validate and authorize at the owning service boundary.
- `resource`: Optional current delivery job/resource when available.

Returns: Exactly true to admit the current operation; false denies.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects underlying service, authorization or persistence failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { ArtifactDeliveryService, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function canEnqueue(options: ConstructorParameters<typeof ArtifactDeliveryService>[0], principal: PluginPrincipal, input: unknown) {
  return await options.authorize(principal, "enqueue_delivery", input) === true;
}
```


#### `execute`

Enqueues, reads, runs, cancels or explicitly recovers one durable approved delivery job.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified current tenant principal; operation/resource admission is rechecked before transitions.
- `op`: One of deliveryOperations; each input is checked by its closed schema.
- `a`: jobId for every operation; enqueue additionally needs commandId/channel/kind/target/contentHash/approvalRequestId, and recovery needs the exact running job revision.

Returns: The durable AtomicRow<DeliveryJob>, possibly an existing identical enqueue receipt or already terminal job; query get_delivery for current state after receipt replay.

### Remarks

Publish starts at build, withdrawal at activate; completion follows successful purge. Cancellation requires a reconciliation port and never removes a newer host version. Completed jobs require a new withdrawal job instead of cancellation. Recovery requires exact revision and drained(old token), marks failed and clears ownership for retry. Failure retains the last durable phase and a sanitized error, while the original host error may reject the call.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid principal/input (401/400), denied live/public approval (403), absent job (404), busy channel/worker, stale recovery or unavailable cancellation port (409), invalid built artifact and propagated repository/port failures; effects may already have occurred.

Example:

```typescript
import { ArtifactDeliveryService, type PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export function readDelivery(service: ArtifactDeliveryService, principal: PluginPrincipal, jobId: string) { return service.execute(principal, 'get_delivery', { jobId }); }
```


#### `execute.a.jobId`

Stable job ID required by every delivery operation; 1–80 letters/digits/underscore/hyphen characters.


#### `execute.a.revision`

Exact current positive running-job revision required only for explicit drained-worker recovery.


#### `execute.a.commandId`

Stable enqueue idempotency ID; identical input replays the original receipt and conflicting reuse rejects.



### Example

```typescript
import { ArtifactDeliveryService } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export function connectDelivery(options: ConstructorParameters<typeof ArtifactDeliveryService>[0]) { return new ArtifactDeliveryService(options); }
```

Checks that a reported migration verification matches its plan and contains only matched in-scope records.

`BackendMigrationVerificationReport`

Validates nonempty records and nonnegative revisions, but does not prove exhaustive tenant/plugin coverage or equal source/target revision numbers. The host owns verification completeness and truth.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     repository: AtomicRepository;     principal: PluginPrincipal;     verifyCurrent: () => Promise<void>;     prefix?: string; }` | Yes | Scoped repository; principal is validated/cloned; verifyCurrent must reject on revoked admission; prefix defaults to graph-checkpoint and must contain 1–64 lowercase letters/digits/underscore/hyphen. |

### Returns

`AtomicCheckpointSaver`

### Remarks

Admission and workflow writer serialization remain host-owned. Each saver instance serializes repository work through an internal Promise chain and calls verifyCurrent before the transaction and before/after its work. This does not serialize other saver instances or whole graph invocations. The repository owns durability/CAS; this saver installs no timers and does not close host storage. Checkpoint erasure requires a separate host retention executor.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

Invalid principal, absent repository/verifier, invalid prefix, or clone failure.

### Public members

#### `constructor.options.repository`

Connected host atomic repository used for scoped checkpoint and pending-write transactions; this saver does not close it.


#### `constructor.options.principal`

Verified plugin principal validated and cloned at construction; fixes the tenant/plugin/user scope used for repository transactions.


#### `constructor.options.verifyCurrent`

Recheck current host admission before repository work and at transaction boundaries.

Returns: No value; resolve only while the captured principal remains admitted and reject when admission is revoked.

### Remarks

Required callback; called before the repository transaction and before/after its work, and before each history yield. The host owns the live policy lookup.

### See also

[AtomicCheckpointSaver](#api-AtomicCheckpointSaver)


#### `constructor.options.prefix`

Optional repository key prefix; defaults to graph-checkpoint and must contain 1–64 lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.


#### `getTuple`

Reads one scoped checkpoint and its separately stored pending writes.

Parameters:

- `config`: LangGraph config with required thread_id, optional checkpoint_ns (default empty), and optional checkpoint_id (default latest lexicographic ID). Identifiers are bounded to 512 characters without control characters.

Returns: Decoded checkpoint tuple or undefined if no selected checkpoint exists.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid identifiers, tenant/thread/namespace or format mismatch, and admission/repository/serialization failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { AtomicCheckpointSaver } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/atomic-checkpointer";
export async function read(saver: AtomicCheckpointSaver, config: Parameters<AtomicCheckpointSaver["getTuple"]>[0]) { return saver.getTuple(config); }
```


#### `list`

Lists scoped checkpoint history in descending lexicographic checkpoint-ID order.

Parameters:

- `config`: Required thread scope, optional namespace, and optional exact checkpoint ID filter.
- `options`: limit defaults to 100 and must be a safe integer 1–2000; before must use the same thread/namespace and excludes its ID and newer IDs; filter compares metadata fields by atomic hash.

Returns: Async sequence of decoded tuples, possibly empty, with admission rechecked before each yield.

### Remarks

History is collected in a bounded repository transaction before yielding; changing authorization can still stop later yields.

### Errors and rejections

Iteration rejects invalid scope/limits, more than 2000 scanned checkpoint rows, identity/format mismatch, or admission/repository/serialization errors.

Example:

```typescript
import { AtomicCheckpointSaver } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/atomic-checkpointer";
export async function history(saver: AtomicCheckpointSaver, config: Parameters<AtomicCheckpointSaver["list"]>[0]) {
  const tuples = [];
  for await (const tuple of saver.list(config, { limit: 10 })) tuples.push(tuple);
  return tuples;
}
```


#### `put`

Writes an immutable version-4 checkpoint and advances the scoped latest pointer when its ID sorts later.

Parameters:

- `config`: Thread/namespace scope; optional checkpoint_id becomes the new checkpoint's parent ID.
- `checkpoint`: Current LangGraph version-4 checkpoint with valid nonempty bounded ID.
- `metadata`: Serializer-supported checkpoint metadata.

Returns: A config selecting the stored checkpoint ID.

### Remarks

Repeating identical content is accepted; latest ordering is lexicographic, so host checkpoint IDs must reflect desired chronology.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects unsupported format, ID reuse with different content, admission/CAS/repository errors, or serialization failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { AtomicCheckpointSaver } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/atomic-checkpointer";
export async function write(saver: AtomicCheckpointSaver, ...args: Parameters<AtomicCheckpointSaver["put"]>) { return saver.put(...args); }
```


#### `putWrites`

Merges pending channel writes by task/index for one scoped checkpoint.

Parameters:

- `config`: Thread/namespace with required checkpoint_id.
- `writes`: At most 256 channel/value pairs; channels are valid bounded identifiers. Ordinary task/index duplicates retain their first value; reserved negative-index channels replace prior values.
- `taskId`: Nonempty bounded task identifier associating writes.

Returns: No value; resolves after the merged writes are durably stored.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects missing checkpoint ID, invalid task/channel, identity mismatch, more than 2000 stored pending writes, or admission/repository/serialization errors.

Example:

```typescript
import { AtomicCheckpointSaver } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/atomic-checkpointer";
export async function writePending(saver: AtomicCheckpointSaver, ...args: Parameters<AtomicCheckpointSaver["putWrites"]>) { await saver.putWrites(...args); }
```


#### `deleteThread`

Rejects thread deletion because this repository contract provides no approved erasure operation.

Parameters:

- `_threadId`: Requested thread ID; not read or deleted.

Returns: No value; this operation always rejects before performing storage work.

### Errors and rejections

Always rejects with an error directing the caller to the host retention executor.

Example:

```typescript
import { AtomicCheckpointSaver } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/atomic-checkpointer";
export async function erase(saver: AtomicCheckpointSaver, threadId: string) {
  try { await saver.deleteThread(threadId); } catch (error) {
    // Host retention tooling must perform reviewed erasure.
    throw error;
  }
}
```



### Example

```typescript
import { AtomicCheckpointSaver } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/atomic-checkpointer";
export function saver(options: ConstructorParameters<typeof AtomicCheckpointSaver>[0]) {
  return new AtomicCheckpointSaver(options);
}
```


<a id="api-atomicCommand"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `atomicCommand`

Replay or atomically record one principal/operation-scoped command result in an existing transaction.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function atomicCommand<T>(tx: AtomicSession, p: PluginPrincipal, operation: string, input: {
    commandId: string;
}, work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Live tenant-scoped atomic session enclosing the actual domain work. |
| `p` | `PluginPrincipal` | Yes | Verified principal whose user ID scopes the command receipt. |
| `operation` | `string` | Yes | Trusted operation name included in the receipt key. |
| `input` | `{     commandId: string; }` | Yes | Complete command input with a commandId of 1–80 letters/digits/underscore/hyphen. |
| `work` | `() => Promise<T>` | Yes | Async domain callback run only for a new command; must remain inside the same transaction. |

### Returns

`Promise<T>`

The existing identical receipt result or the newly computed result.

### Type parameters

- `T`: JSON-serializable domain result stored and returned by the command receipt.

### Remarks

Caller performs live resource authorization before replay as well as execution. Domain writes, receipt and audit share the existing transaction; irreversible external effects must be durably queued, not performed inside work.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects malformed command IDs, input reuse with a different hash, CAS/audit failures and propagated work errors.

### Public members

#### `input.commandId`

Stable nonempty 1–80 character command ID scoped by actor and operation; identical full input replays the stored result.



### Example

```typescript
import { atomicCommand, type AtomicRepository, type AtomicSession, type PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data'
export function command<T>(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal, input: { commandId: string }, work: (session: AtomicSession) => Promise<T>) {
 // The host performs live resource admission before replay or new execution.
 return repository.run(principal, session => atomicCommand(session, principal, 'example-operation', input, () => work(session)))
}
```

Optional dispatcher clock; createAtomicOutboxDispatcher forwards it, while standalone store.claim uses its explicit now parameter.

<a id="api-AtomicRepository"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AtomicRepository`

Host-admitted transactional entrypoint that scopes all session operations to one verified principal.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AtomicRepository {
    run<T>(principal: PluginPrincipal, work: (session: AtomicSession) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | `Promise<T>` | Yes | Runs work in one verified tenant transaction whose session expires when work settles. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createAtomicRepository for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `run`

Runs work in one verified tenant transaction whose session expires when work settles.

Parameters:

- `principal`: Verified tenant/user principal; repository structure checks do not prove live permission.
- `work`: Async domain work; never let session or joined SQL capabilities escape its lifetime.

Returns: The callback result after successful commit; work/commit failure rejects and triggers rollback.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Value resolved by the transaction/connection callback.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects propagated host persistence, validation or callback failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicRepository, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function updateTitle(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal, id: string, title: string) {
  return repository.run(principal, async session => {
    const current = await session.get<{ title: string }>(id);
    if (!current) throw new Error("Record unavailable");
    return session.put(id, { title }, current.revision);
  });
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-AtomicSession"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AtomicSession`

Temporary tenant/namespace-bound session valid only inside its repository work callback.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AtomicSession {
    get<T>(id: string): Promise<AtomicRow<T> | null>;
    getMany?<T>(ids: string[]): Promise<(AtomicRow<T> | null)[]>;
    putMany?<T>(changes: {
        id: string;
        value: T;
        expected: number;
    }[]): Promise<AtomicRow<T>[]>;
    list<T>(prefix: string, after?: string, limit?: number): Promise<AtomicRow<T>[]>;
    put<T>(id: string, value: T, expected: number): Promise<AtomicRow<T>>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get` | `Promise<AtomicRow<T> \| null>` | Yes | Performs one scoped read inside the active repository transaction. |
| `getMany` | `Promise<(AtomicRow<T> \| null)[]>` | No | Performs ordered batch reads inside the active repository transaction.  Batch reads preserve tenant scope and input order; missing rows are null. |
| `putMany` | `Promise<AtomicRow<T>[]>` | No | Performs transactional batch CAS writes inside the active repository transaction.  Every item uses CAS in the enclosing transaction; any failure rolls back all items. |
| `list` | `Promise<AtomicRow<T>[]>` | Yes | Performs a bounded scoped keyset read inside the active repository transaction.  Empty prefix reads the repository's own tenant/namespace, never another tenant. |
| `put` | `Promise<AtomicRow<T>>` | Yes | Performs one create-or-CAS write inside the active repository transaction.  expected=0 creates; otherwise atomically replaces exactly the expected revision. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createAtomicRepository for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `get`

Performs one scoped read inside the active repository transaction.

Parameters:

- `id`: Logical row ID; 1–240 supported record-key characters.

Returns: The scoped envelope or null when absent.

### Type parameters

- `T`: JSON payload type read or persisted by this session operation.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects expired session, invalid IDs/revisions/limits, document/payload errors, duplicate/create or CAS conflict and provider failures as applicable.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicRepository, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function readTitle(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal, id: string) {
  return repository.run(principal, async session => {
    const row = await session.get<{ title: string }>(id);
    return row?.value.title ?? null;
  });
}
```


#### `getMany`

Performs ordered batch reads inside the active repository transaction.

Batch reads preserve tenant scope and input order; missing rows are null.

Parameters:

- `ids`: Logical IDs in desired output order; duplicates retain their positions.

Returns: One envelope or null per input ID in the same order.

### Type parameters

- `T`: JSON payload type read or persisted by this session operation.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects expired session, invalid IDs/revisions/limits, document/payload errors, duplicate/create or CAS conflict and provider failures as applicable.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicRepository, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function readTitles(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal, ids: string[]) {
  return repository.run(principal, async session => {
    if (!session.getMany) throw new Error("Batch reads not supported");
    return session.getMany<{ title: string }>(ids);
  });
}
```


#### `putMany`

Performs transactional batch CAS writes inside the active repository transaction.

Every item uses CAS in the enclosing transaction; any failure rolls back all items.

Parameters:

- `changes`: Unique logical-ID/value/expected changes; expected=0 creates and positive expected performs exact CAS.

Returns: Next-revision envelopes in input order; any failure must reject the enclosing transaction.

### Type parameters

- `T`: JSON payload type read or persisted by this session operation.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects expired session, invalid IDs/revisions/limits, document/payload errors, duplicate/create or CAS conflict and provider failures as applicable.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicRepository, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function createPair(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal) {
  return repository.run(principal, async session => {
    if (!session.putMany) throw new Error("Batch writes not supported");
    return session.putMany([{ id: "examples/first", value: { title: "First" }, expected: 0 }, { id: "examples/second", value: { title: "Second" }, expected: 0 }]);
  });
}
```


#### `putMany.changes[].id`

Unique logical record key within this batch and tenant namespace.


#### `putMany.changes[].value`

JSON payload to validate against configured policy/document contracts.


#### `putMany.changes[].expected`

Expected safe CAS revision; 0 creates, positive values replace exactly that revision.


#### `list`

Performs a bounded scoped keyset read inside the active repository transaction.

Empty prefix reads the repository's own tenant/namespace, never another tenant.

Parameters:

- `prefix`: Logical prefix; empty stays within this repository tenant/namespace.
- `after`: Optional exclusive logical ID; defaults to the start of the prefix range.
- `limit`: Integer page size 1–101; defaults to 100.

Returns: Envelopes in stable logical-ID order within the prefix.

### Type parameters

- `T`: JSON payload type read or persisted by this session operation.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects expired session, invalid IDs/revisions/limits, document/payload errors, duplicate/create or CAS conflict and provider failures as applicable.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicRepository, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function firstPage(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal) {
  return repository.run(principal, session => session.list<{ title: string }>("examples/", "", 20));
}
```


#### `put`

Performs one create-or-CAS write inside the active repository transaction.

expected=0 creates; otherwise atomically replaces exactly the expected revision.

Parameters:

- `id`: Logical row ID.
- `value`: JSON payload admitted by configured limits/contracts.
- `expected`: Safe integer expected revision from 0 to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER-1; 0 creates, otherwise exact CAS.

Returns: A cloned-payload envelope with revision expected+1.

### Type parameters

- `T`: JSON payload type read or persisted by this session operation.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects expired session, invalid IDs/revisions/limits, document/payload errors, duplicate/create or CAS conflict and provider failures as applicable.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicRepository, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function createTitle(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal, id: string, title: string) {
  return repository.run(principal, session => session.put(id, { title }, 0));
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

## [INTERFACE] `AtomicSqlConnection`

Connection-bound SQL operations sharing the enclosing commit/rollback boundary.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AtomicSqlConnection {
    execute(sql: string, binds: unknown[]): Promise<{
        rows?: Record<string, unknown>[];
        affectedRows: number;
    }>;
    executeMany?(sql: string, binds: unknown[][]): Promise<{

    }>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `execute` | `Promise<{     rows?: Record<string, unknown>[];     affectedRows: number; }>` | Yes | Executes one trusted SQL statement on the exact connection owning the enclosing transaction. |
| `executeMany` | `Promise<{     affectedRows: number[]; }>` | No | Optionally executes ordered bind batches on the same transaction connection. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createAtomicRepository for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `execute`

Executes one trusted SQL statement on the exact connection owning the enclosing transaction.

Parameters:

- `sql`: Trusted parameterized SQL with tenant/namespace predicates.
- `binds`: Positional bind values in placeholder order.

Returns: Optional query rows and an accurate affected-row count.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects propagated host persistence, validation or callback failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicSqlDriver, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function queryJoined(driver: AtomicSqlDriver, principal: PluginPrincipal, trustedTenantSql: string, bindings: unknown[]) {
  return driver.transaction(principal, async connection => {
    return (await connection.execute(trustedTenantSql, bindings)).rows ?? [];
  });
}
```


#### `execute.rows`

Optional object rows from SELECT execution on this connection.


#### `execute.affectedRows`

Accurate affected-row count for scalar execution or one count per ordered batch bind row.


#### `executeMany`

Optionally executes ordered bind batches on the same transaction connection.

Parameters:

- `sql`: Trusted parameterized DML.
- `binds`: Ordered positional bind rows.

Returns: An affectedRows count for every bind row in input order; missing/wrong counts must fail CAS.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects propagated host persistence, validation or callback failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicSqlDriver, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function batchReviewed(driver: AtomicSqlDriver, principal: PluginPrincipal, trustedTenantDml: string, binds: unknown[][]) {
  return driver.transaction(principal, async connection => {
    if (!connection.executeMany) throw new Error("Batch DML not supported");
    return (await connection.executeMany(trustedTenantDml, binds)).affectedRows;
  });
}
```


#### `executeMany.affectedRows`

Accurate affected-row count for scalar execution or one count per ordered batch bind row.

<a id="api-AtomicSqlDriver"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AtomicSqlDriver`

Provider transaction boundary required for envelope CAS, domain writes and durable journal atomicity.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AtomicSqlDriver {
    dialect: 'sqlite' | 'oracle' | 'postgres';
    transaction<T>(principal: PluginPrincipal, work: (connection: AtomicSqlConnection) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dialect` | `'sqlite' \| 'oracle' \| 'postgres'` | Yes | SQL placeholder/driver dialect selected by trusted host configuration. |
| `transaction` | `Promise<T>` | Yes | Acquires one transaction connection, commits success and rolls back rejection.  Same connection for every statement; commits on success, rolls back on rejection. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createAtomicRepository for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `dialect`

SQL placeholder/driver dialect selected by trusted host configuration.


#### `transaction`

Acquires one transaction connection, commits success and rolls back rejection.

Same connection for every statement; commits on success, rolls back on rejection.

Parameters:

- `principal`: Verified tenant/user principal used for host session admission.
- `work`: Async work on the same connection for every domain/CAS/audit statement.

Returns: The callback result after commit; all joined writes roll back on failure.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Value resolved by the transaction/connection callback.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects propagated host persistence, validation or callback failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AtomicSqlDriver, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function readJoined(driver: AtomicSqlDriver, principal: PluginPrincipal, trustedTenantSql: string, bindings: unknown[]) {
  return driver.transaction(principal, async connection => {
    const result = await connection.execute(trustedTenantSql, bindings);
    return result.rows ?? [];
  });
}
```

<a id="api-AuthSessionVerifier"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `AuthSessionVerifier`

Host authentication adapters used by [createAuthMiddleware](#api-createAuthMiddleware).

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/middleware/auth`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface AuthSessionVerifier {
    verifySession(authHeader?: string, cookieHeader?: string): Promise<{
        valid: boolean;
        userId?: string;
        email?: string;
        tenantId?: string;
        isSuperAdmin?: boolean;
        pendingApproval?: boolean;
        pendingId?: string;
        user?: EaosUser;
    }>;
    verifyApiKey?(token: string): Promise<{
        valid: boolean;
        tenantId?: string;
        userId?: string;
    }> | {
        valid: boolean;
        tenantId?: string;
        userId?: string;
    };
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verifySession` | `Promise<{     valid: boolean;     userId?: string;     email?: string;     tenantId?: string;     isSuperAdmin?: boolean;     pendingApproval?: boolean;     pendingId?: string;     user?: EaosUser; }>` | Yes | Verifies a session before the optional API key fallback. |
| `verifyApiKey` | `Promise<{     valid: boolean;     tenantId?: string;     userId?: string; }> \| {     valid: boolean;     tenantId?: string;     userId?: string; }` | No | Verifies a nonempty credential after session verification fails. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Remarks

Results must come from verified credentials and trusted membership data; this middleware does not independently validate claims.

### Public members

#### `verifySession`

Verifies a session before the optional API key fallback.

Parameters:

- `authHeader`: Raw Authorization header, or undefined if absent.
- `cookieHeader`: Raw Cookie header, or undefined if absent.

Returns: Session validity and trusted optional identity claims. pendingApproval takes priority over valid and produces 403.

### Errors and rejections

Rejections propagate through request handling.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AuthSessionVerifier } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function inspectSession(verifier: AuthSessionVerifier, request: Request) {
  // The host verifier checks real credentials; a header alone is not trusted.
  const result = await verifier.verifySession(
    request.headers.get("Authorization") ?? undefined,
    request.headers.get("Cookie") ?? undefined,
  );
  return { valid: result.valid, pendingApproval: result.pendingApproval === true };
}
```


#### `verifySession.valid`

True only after successful trusted credential verification.


#### `verifySession.userId`

Optional authenticated user ID copied to Hono context.


#### `verifySession.email`

Optional verified email used when synthesizing a user object.


#### `verifySession.tenantId`

Optional verified tenant claim; session middleware can continue without it, so downstream tenant admission remains required.


#### `verifySession.isSuperAdmin`

Trusted platform authority enabling X-Tenant-Id selection and synthesized super_admin role.


#### `verifySession.pendingApproval`

When truthy, produces a 403 before session validity or API-key fallback is considered.


#### `verifySession.pendingId`

Optional approval reference included in a pending response.


#### `verifySession.user`

Optional trusted user object copied unchanged; if omitted with userId, middleware synthesizes one.


#### `verifyApiKey`

Verifies a nonempty credential after session verification fails.

Parameters:

- `token`: Authorization value with a leading Bearer prefix removed case-insensitively.

Returns: Validity and trusted identity claims; a valid result also needs tenantId to grant access.

### Errors and rejections

Adapter errors propagate through request handling.

Example:

```typescript
import type { AuthSessionVerifier } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function inspectApiKey(verifier: AuthSessionVerifier, token: string) {
  if (!verifier.verifyApiKey) throw new Error("Host API-key verification is unavailable");
  // Supply the actual credential without logging or persisting it here.
  const result = await verifier.verifyApiKey(token);
  return result.valid && !!result.tenantId;
}
```


#### `verifyApiKey.valid`

True for a verified API key; tenantId is additionally required to continue.


#### `verifyApiKey.tenantId`

Required tenant claim for a successful middleware API-key fallback.


#### `verifyApiKey.userId`

Optional authenticated key owner copied to userId; no user object is synthesized for this path.


#### `verifyApiKey.valid`

True only when the host has verified the presented API key; middleware also requires a truthy tenantId before continuing.


#### `verifyApiKey.tenantId`

Trusted tenant claim required for successful API-key fallback; middleware does not verify tenant membership independently.


#### `verifyApiKey.userId`

Optional verified key-owner identity copied to request context; this fallback does not synthesize an EaosUser object.



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-buildSystemdRunArgs"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `buildSystemdRunArgs`

Builds systemd-run arguments for transient process resource and filesystem restrictions.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/executor`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function buildSystemdRunArgs(command: string, args: readonly string[], policy: AgentRuntimeResourcePolicy, cwd: string | undefined, unit: string): string[];
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | `string` | Yes | Trusted executable passed after the systemd option terminator. |
| `args` | `readonly string[]` | Yes | Executable arguments, passed unchanged without a shell. |
| `policy` | `AgentRuntimeResourcePolicy` | Yes | Already validated resource policy; this helper does not validate it. |
| `cwd` | `string \| undefined` | Yes | Working directory, resolved absolutely; absent/empty uses process.cwd(). |
| `unit` | `string` | Yes | Host-selected transient unit name, used for later stop requests. |

### Returns

`string[]`

A new argument array, using --user for a nonroot host user and rounding runtime milliseconds upward to at least one second.

### Remarks

Requires a host with systemd-run and appropriate service-manager permissions when executed. This array does not implement network allowlisting, workspace capacity, or a concurrency scheduler; those policy fields require host enforcement.

### Example

```typescript
import { defaultRuntimePlacementPolicy } from "@alneas/eaos-core";
import { buildSystemdRunArgs } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/executor";
const args = buildSystemdRunArgs("agent-runtime", ["--version"], defaultRuntimePlacementPolicy().ai.agentRuntime, undefined, "example-agent");
console.log(args.includes("--wait")); // true
```

<a id="api-cancelAgentJob"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `cancelAgentJob`

Marks an owned unstarted job cancelled in the caller's atomic session.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function cancelAgentJob(tx: AtomicSession, principal: PluginPrincipal, jobId: string, now?: Date): Promise<AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Authorized atomic session; caller commits/rolls back. |
| `principal` | `PluginPrincipal` | Yes | Verified tenant/user who owns the job. |
| `jobId` | `string` | Yes | Stored queue job identifier. |
| `now` | `Date` | No | Cancellation timestamp; defaults to a fresh Date. |

### Returns

`Promise<AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>>`

A cloned cancelled job, unchanged when already cancelled.

### Remarks

Running leases cannot be interrupted by this edit. This function performs no external runtime cancellation, approval-ticket revocation, or live admission callback.

### Errors and rejections

Missing/foreign job, request integrity mismatch, status other than queued/retryable/waiting_approval/cancelled, or transaction/clock errors.

### Example

```typescript
import { cancelAgentJob } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs";
import type { AtomicSession } from "@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic";
import type { PluginPrincipal } from "@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data";
export async function cancel(tx: AtomicSession, principal: PluginPrincipal, jobId: string) { return cancelAgentJob(tx, principal, jobId); }
```


<a id="api-canonical"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `canonical`

Serializes JSON-compatible lifecycle values with recursively sorted object keys.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle-engine`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function canonical(value: unknown): string;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `unknown` | Yes | JSON-serializable primitives, arrays or plain/null-prototype objects; avoid cycles and nonfinite numbers. |

### Returns

`string`

Deterministic JSON text; array order is preserved.

### Remarks

Uses JSON.stringify primitive semantics, including null for nonfinite numbers. It does not accept undefined/function/symbol values or class instances. Cyclic graphs are unsupported.

### Errors and rejections

Error for unsupported values/prototypes, JSON serialization failure or recursive cycles.

### Example

```typescript
import { canonical } from '@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle-engine';
const serialized = canonical({ b: [2, 1], a: true });
```

Structural subset of the D1 prepared-statement API used by the record adapter.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface CloudflareD1PreparedStatement {
    bind(...values: unknown[]): CloudflareD1PreparedStatement;

        };

            changes?: number;
        };
    }>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bind` | `CloudflareD1PreparedStatement` | Yes | Binds positional query values to a prepared Worker D1 statement. |
| `all` | `Promise<{     results?: T[];     meta?: {         changes?: number;     }; }>` | Yes | Executes a prepared D1 read and resolves its structural query result. |
| `run` | `Promise<{     meta?: {         changes?: number;     }; }>` | Yes | Executes a prepared D1 write and resolves provider change metadata. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createCloudflareD1Driver for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `bind`

Binds positional query values to a prepared Worker D1 statement.

Parameters:

- `values`: Positional values in SQL placeholder order.

Returns: The bound prepared statement used for all/run.

### Errors and rejections

Provider binding errors throw synchronously.

Example:

```typescript
import type { CloudflareD1Binding } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function readProjection(db: CloudflareD1Binding, tenantId: string) {
  const statement = db.prepare("SELECT ? AS tenant_id").bind(tenantId);
  return (await statement.all<{ tenant_id: string }>()).results ?? [];
}
```


#### `all`

Executes a prepared D1 read and resolves its structural query result.

Returns: Optional typed results and provider change metadata.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Returned query row shape; defaults to a string-keyed unknown-value record.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects provider query failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { CloudflareD1Binding } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function projection(db: CloudflareD1Binding, tenantId: string) {
  const result = await db.prepare("SELECT ? AS tenant_id").bind(tenantId).all<{ tenant_id: string }>();
  return result.results ?? [];
}
```


#### `all.results`

Optional query rows with the caller-selected row shape.


#### `all.meta`

Optional provider execution metadata.


#### `all.meta.changes`

Optional provider affected-row count; record driver normalizes absence to 0.


#### `run`

Executes a prepared D1 write and resolves provider change metadata.

Returns: Optional meta.changes affected-row metadata.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects provider execution failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { CloudflareD1Binding } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function executeReviewed(db: CloudflareD1Binding, trustedTenantDml: string, bindings: unknown[]) {
  // Supply parameterized DML whose bindings include the authorized tenant.
  const result = await db.prepare(trustedTenantDml).bind(...bindings).run();
  return result.meta?.changes ?? 0;
}
```


#### `run.meta`

Optional provider execution metadata.


#### `run.meta.changes`

Optional provider affected-row count; record driver normalizes absence to 0.

<a id="api-CommandHost"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `CommandHost`

Host persistence, transaction and live authorization ports for aggregate command execution.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/commands`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface CommandHost<T extends CommandState> {
    store?: PluginRecordStore<T>;
    transaction?<R>(principal: PluginPrincipal, work: (store: PluginRecordStore<T>) => Promise<R>): Promise<R>;
    authorize(p: PluginPrincipal, operation: string, input: unknown, current?: Readonly<T>): Promise<boolean>;
    now?: () => Date;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `store` | `PluginRecordStore<T>` | No | Optional durable tenant record store; used when transaction is absent. |
| `transaction` | `Promise<R>` | No | Runs aggregate reads, CAS and final permission checks through one real connection-bound transaction.  Trusted connection-bound store; all reads, CAS and final authorization share one transaction. May expose an unstored projection at revision 0; the first write creates revision 1. |
| `authorize` | `Promise<boolean>` | Yes | Checks current lifecycle and permission for the operation and complete returned aggregate.  Must check live activation and access to the entire returned aggregate, including referenced resources. |
| `now` | `() => Date` | No | Optional trusted clock used for operation history timestamps; defaults to new Date(). |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Tenant-owned aggregate state required by the store and reducer transaction.

### See also

RecordCommandService for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `store`

Optional durable tenant record store; used when transaction is absent.


#### `transaction`

Runs aggregate reads, CAS and final permission checks through one real connection-bound transaction.

Trusted connection-bound store; all reads, CAS and final authorization share one transaction.
May expose an unstored projection at revision 0; the first write creates revision 1.

Parameters:

- `principal`: Verified current principal owning the transaction.
- `work`: Async service work receiving the joined record store; do not retain that store after completion.

Returns: The callback result after commit; rejection rolls back joined writes.

### Type parameters

- `R`: Value resolved by the transaction/connection callback.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects propagated host persistence, validation or callback failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { CommandHost, CommandState, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function readAggregate(host: CommandHost<CommandState>, principal: PluginPrincipal, recordId: string) {
  if (!host.transaction) throw new Error("Joined transaction port required");
  return host.transaction(principal, store => store.read(principal.tenantId, recordId));
}
```


#### `authorize`

Checks current lifecycle and permission for the operation and complete returned aggregate.

Must check live activation and access to the entire returned aggregate, including referenced resources.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified principal copied for this check.
- `operation`: Declared operation name.
- `input`: Schema input (initial admission occurs before schema validation).
- `current`: Optional copied current aggregate including all referenced-resource access.

Returns: Exactly true to admit; false denies with PluginError 403.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects propagated host persistence, validation or callback failures.

Example:

```typescript
import type { CommandHost, CommandState, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function canOperate(host: CommandHost<CommandState>, principal: PluginPrincipal, operation: string, input: unknown, current: Readonly<CommandState>) {
  return await host.authorize(principal, operation, input, current) === true;
}
```


#### `now`

Optional trusted clock used for operation history timestamps; defaults to new Date().

Returns: A valid Date whose toISOString value becomes the operation timestamp.

### Errors and rejections

Callback failures propagate to the owning operation; transactional writes roll back when the host boundary rejects.



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.
