<a id="api-DeliveryPorts"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `DeliveryPorts`

Host publication approval, immutable artifact and idempotent external delivery capabilities.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/delivery`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface DeliveryPorts {
    verify(p: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryRequest): Promise<boolean>;
    build(p: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob): Promise<DeliveryArtifact>;
    activate(p: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob): Promise<void>;
    purge(p: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob): Promise<void>;
    cancel?(p: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob): Promise<void>;
    drained?(p: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob): Promise<boolean>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verify` | `Promise<boolean>` | Yes | Verify public publication/withdrawal approval for the exact target and content.  Verify explicit PUBLIC publication (or withdrawal) permission, exact target/hash and approval. Ordinary reader access is insufficient. |
| `build` | `Promise<DeliveryArtifact>` | Yes | Build and stage an immutable artifact outside the database transaction.  Build and stage an immutable artifact outside a DB transaction. Must be idempotent for jobId. |
| `activate` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Apply or withdraw the exact public channel version idempotently.  Atomic, idempotent channel update/withdrawal. Serialize with other host publishers; key=jobId. |
| `purge` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Invalidate the delivered channel idempotently before recording completion.  Idempotent CDN invalidation; completion is recorded only after success. |
| `cancel` | `Promise<void>` | No | Reconcile uncertain job effects and purge only this job's owned version.  Reconcile any uncertain activation for this job and purge it, idempotently. Never remove a newer publisher's version. |
| `drained` | `Promise<boolean>` | No | Prove prior workers for this job token can no longer perform effects. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

ArtifactDeliveryService for canonical host integration.

### Public members

#### `verify`

Verify public publication/withdrawal approval for the exact target and content.

Verify explicit PUBLIC publication (or withdrawal) permission, exact target/hash and approval. Ordinary reader access is insufficient.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified principal requiring explicit public publication/withdrawal permission.
- `job`: Pinned request/job with exact approved target/contentHash/approvalRequestId.

Returns: Exactly true only when public permission and exact binding/approval remain valid.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host permission, artifact, delivery or worker-control failures; external effects may already be partially complete.

Example:

```typescript
import type { DeliveryPorts, DeliveryRequest, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function verifyReviewed(ports: DeliveryPorts, principal: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryRequest) {
  // The host binds permission and external effects to this exact job.
  return ports.verify(principal, job);
}
```


#### `build`

Build and stage an immutable artifact outside the database transaction.

Build and stage an immutable artifact outside a DB transaction. Must be idempotent for jobId.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified current principal.
- `job`: Durable job carrying the stable jobId idempotency identity.

Returns: An immutable staged artifact key, lowercase hash and positive safe byte size.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host permission, artifact, delivery or worker-control failures; external effects may already be partially complete.

Example:

```typescript
import type { DeliveryPorts, DeliveryJob, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function buildReviewed(ports: DeliveryPorts, principal: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob) {
  // The host binds permission and external effects to this exact job.
  return ports.build(principal, job);
}
```


#### `activate`

Apply or withdraw the exact public channel version idempotently.

Atomic, idempotent channel update/withdrawal. Serialize with other host publishers; key=jobId.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified current principal.
- `job`: Exact pinned publish/withdraw job, including staged artifact when publishing.

Returns: Resolves without a value after the idempotent channel switch/withdrawal.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host permission, artifact, delivery or worker-control failures; external effects may already be partially complete.

Example:

```typescript
import type { DeliveryPorts, DeliveryJob, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function activateReviewed(ports: DeliveryPorts, principal: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob) {
  // The host binds permission and external effects to this exact job.
  await ports.activate(principal, job);
}
```


#### `purge`

Invalidate the delivered channel idempotently before recording completion.

Idempotent CDN invalidation; completion is recorded only after success.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified current principal.
- `job`: Exact job channel/version requiring invalidation.

Returns: Resolves without a value only after actual idempotent invalidation succeeds.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host permission, artifact, delivery or worker-control failures; external effects may already be partially complete.

Example:

```typescript
import type { DeliveryPorts, DeliveryJob, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function purgeReviewed(ports: DeliveryPorts, principal: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob) {
  // The host binds permission and external effects to this exact job.
  await ports.purge(principal, job);
}
```


#### `cancel`

Reconcile uncertain job effects and purge only this job's owned version.

Reconcile any uncertain activation for this job and purge it, idempotently. Never remove a newer publisher's version.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified current principal admitted for cancellation.
- `job`: Pinned job whose uncertain effects need reconciliation.

Returns: Resolves without a value after idempotent reconciliation/purge of only this owned version; never remove newer publications.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host permission, artifact, delivery or worker-control failures; external effects may already be partially complete.

Example:

```typescript
import type { DeliveryPorts, DeliveryJob, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function cancelReviewed(ports: DeliveryPorts, principal: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob) {
  if (!ports.cancel) throw new Error("Required recovery port unavailable");
  // The host binds permission and external effects to this exact job.
  await ports.cancel(principal, job);
}
```


#### `drained`

Prove prior workers for this job token can no longer perform effects.

Parameters:

- `p`: Verified principal admitted for recovery.
- `job`: Exact running job revision/token whose prior workers must be stopped.

Returns: Exactly true only when prior workers cannot perform further effects; false/absence prevents recovery.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host permission, artifact, delivery or worker-control failures; external effects may already be partially complete.

Example:

```typescript
import type { DeliveryPorts, DeliveryJob, PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data';
export async function drainedReviewed(ports: DeliveryPorts, principal: PluginPrincipal, job: DeliveryJob) {
  if (!ports.drained) throw new Error("Required recovery port unavailable");
  // The host binds permission and external effects to this exact job.
  return ports.drained(principal, job);
}
```

<a id="api-deploymentExecutionTarget"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `deploymentExecutionTarget`

Builds a scoped task target from a reviewed destination and the current inspection context.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/platform`, `@alneas/eaos-server/platform/deployment-placements`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function deploymentExecutionTarget(destination: DeploymentDestination, scope: 'environment' | 'tenant', context?: DeploymentTarget): DeploymentTarget | undefined;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `destination` | `DeploymentDestination` | Yes | Validated destination with optional exact database and dedicated-tenant identities. |
| `scope` | `'environment' \| 'tenant'` | Yes | Environment work omits tenant; tenant work requires a matching concrete tenant. |
| `context` | `DeploymentTarget` | No | Current environment/tenant context; omitted cannot resolve a target. |

### Returns

`DeploymentTarget \| undefined`

A new target object, or undefined for missing context/tenant or dedicated-tenant mismatch.

### Remarks

Backend/database come from the destination, not the context. This performs no authority or resource-existence checks.

### Example

```typescript
import { deploymentExecutionTarget } from '@alneas/eaos-server/platform/deployment-placements';
const target = deploymentExecutionTarget({ id: 'web', placement: 'host', service: 'frontend', revision: '1' }, 'environment', { environment: 'review' });
```

<a id="api-deploymentPlacementHash"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `deploymentPlacementHash`

Hashes a selected plugin's normalized component destinations and host binding revisions.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/platform`, `@alneas/eaos-server/platform/deployment-placements`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function deploymentPlacementHash(placements: DeploymentPlacements, owner: string, pluginId: string, bindings?: Record<string, string>): string;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placements` | `DeploymentPlacements` | Yes | Previously validated placement declaration. |
| `owner` | `string` | Yes | Inventory owner selecting the plugin. |
| `pluginId` | `string` | Yes | Selected plugin ID. |
| `bindings` | `Record<string, string>` | No | Optional nonsecret destination-ID to host-binding revision map; defaults to none. |

### Returns

`string`

A lowercase SHA-256 hash bound to selected components, referenced destinations and applicable binding revisions.

### Remarks

Order of component/destination maps is normalized. Change binding revisions when provider credentials or host wiring change so old scoped evidence becomes stale.

### Errors and rejections

Error when the owner/plugin selection is absent or canonical serialization fails.

### Example

```typescript
import { deploymentPlacementHash, type DeploymentPlacements } from '@alneas/eaos-server/platform/deployment-placements';
export function bindingDigest(placements: DeploymentPlacements, owner: string, pluginId: string) { return deploymentPlacementHash(placements, owner, pluginId); }
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Live tenant-scoped atomic session inside the owner's atomicCommand. |
| `p` | `PluginPrincipal` | Yes | Verified document reader principal. |
| `target` | `AnnotationTarget` | Yes | Pinned document scope hash and its admitted anchor/check IDs. |
| `operation` | `string` | Yes | One of annotationOperations. |
| `a` | `Record<string, any>` | Yes | Input already validated against the selected annotation schema. |
| `now` | `string` | Yes | Trusted ISO timestamp used for newly created comments. |

### Returns

`Promise<{     revision: number;     canResolve: boolean;     id: string;     anchorId: string \| null;     body: string;     visibility: "private" \| "shared";     authorId: string;     createdAt: string;     resolved: boolean; } \| {     cursor?: string \| undefined;     checkIds: readonly string[];     checks: Record<string, boolean>;     revision: number;     comments: {         revision: number;         canResolve: boolean;         id: string;         anchorId: string \| null;         body: string;         visibility: "private" \| "shared";         authorId: string;         createdAt: string;         resolved: boolean;     }[]; } \| {     checks: {         [x: string]: boolean;     };     revision: number; }>`

Operation-specific checks, comment or page data with CAS revisions and optional scoped cursor.

### Remarks

Does not enforce the outer schema or own authorization/transaction/table creation. The owner must authorize the exact document and wrap write operations in atomicCommand; private/shared visibility is scoped by user and document hash.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid scope/cursors, unknown checks/anchors/operations, comment ownership violations, missing comments, capacity or CAS conflicts.

### Example

```typescript
import { documentAnnotations } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data'
export function readComments(tx: Parameters<typeof documentAnnotations>[0], p: Parameters<typeof documentAnnotations>[1], target: Parameters<typeof documentAnnotations>[2], now: string) { return documentAnnotations(tx, p, target, 'get_annotations', { visibility: 'private' }, now) }
```

<a id="api-DurableAgentJobDispatcher"></a>

## [CLASS] `DurableAgentJobDispatcher`

Durable boundary between Micro 2 and an ARM agent runtime.

The store is host-owned and must persist leases, attempts and results. This
class owns only one bounded pass; a host scheduler calls runOnce again.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class DurableAgentJobDispatcher {
    constructor(options: AgentJobDispatcherOptions);
    runOnce(): Promise<AgentJobDispatchResult>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `AgentJobDispatcherOptions` | Yes | Store/worker plus bounded batch, attempt, delay, clock, and completion settings. |

### Returns

`DurableAgentJobDispatcher`

### Remarks

Jobs execute sequentially within each pass, but concurrent runOnce calls are not serialized here. Leases and admission must be enforced by the host store. Completion callbacks run before markCompleted and can be repeated after retry; make external effects idempotent.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

Missing store/worker, batchSize/maxAttempts outside safe integer 1–100, or nonfinite/negative/inverted retry delays.

### Public members

#### `runOnce`

Claims one batch and executes jobs sequentially, persisting completion, approval wait, retry, or failure.

Returns: Per-outcome counts after all claimed jobs have been processed.

### Remarks

Retry delay is min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1)), using job.attempt + 1 for the attempt calculation. No timer or automatic second pass is installed. Results marked PENDING_APPROVAL do not count as success.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects claim/transition/clock failures; worker errors become retryable failure results. Completion callback/markCompleted errors trigger retry-or-fail handling.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableAgentJobDispatcher, type AgentJobDispatcherOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs";
export async function runOnce(options: AgentJobDispatcherOptions) { return new DurableAgentJobDispatcher(options).runOnce(); }
```



### Example

```typescript
import { DurableAgentJobDispatcher, type AgentJobDispatcherOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs";
export async function dispatch(options: AgentJobDispatcherOptions) {
  return new DurableAgentJobDispatcher(options).runOnce();
}
```


<a id="api-DurableAIExecutionBroker"></a>

## [CLASS] `DurableAIExecutionBroker`

Micro2 controller for dynamic model/runtime allocation.

It selects only host-advertised routes and persists the selected route in
the durable job. It never reads a subscription credential or starts a local
process. A local-pull route is later claimed by LocalRunnerPullCoordinator.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class DurableAIExecutionBroker {
    constructor(options: {
        routes: readonly ServerAIExecutionRoute[];
        policyVersion?: string;
        now?: () => Date;
    });
    listRoutes(): readonly ServerAIExecutionRoute[];
    decide(request: AIExecutionRequest): AIExecutionDecision;
    plan(input: AIJobSubmission): AIJobPlan;
    enqueue(tx: AtomicSession, input: AIJobSubmission): Promise<AIJobPlan>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     routes: readonly ServerAIExecutionRoute[];     policyVersion?: string;     now?: () => Date; }` | Yes | Nonempty routes list; optional policyVersion labels selector decisions and now supplies job timestamps, defaulting to fresh Date. |

### Returns

`DurableAIExecutionBroker`

### Remarks

Route selection and planning are process-local. The host verifies identity and supplies current candidate availability/policy; authorization, runtime execution, and safe retries remain separate responsibilities.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

Invalid/missing routes, incompatible local dispatch bindings, core selector validation, or clone failures.

### Public members

#### `constructor.options.routes`

Nonempty host-approved execution routes, validated/cloned before configuring the selector; route IDs and runtime dispatch bindings must be compatible.


#### `constructor.options.policyVersion`

Optional decision policy label forwarded to the Core selector; omission selects ai-execution-policy-v1.


#### `constructor.options.now`

Optional clock used when constructing agent job records; omission creates a new current Date per call.

Returns: A valid Date used for planned job timestamps; clock failures propagate from planning.

### See also

[DurableAIExecutionBroker.plan](#api-DurableAIExecutionBroker)


#### `listRoutes`

Lists registered server route bindings without exposing mutable stored objects.

Returns: Cloned route records in registration map order.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableAIExecutionBroker } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
export function routes(broker: DurableAIExecutionBroker) { return broker.listRoutes(); }
```


#### `decide`

Selects an eligible host-advertised runtime using the core routing policy.

Parameters:

- `request`: Verified AI execution requirements and context.

Returns: The core selector decision; no job is persisted or runtime started.

### Errors and rejections

Propagates core routing validation/no-eligible-route errors.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableAIExecutionBroker } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
import type { AIExecutionRequest } from "@alneas/eaos-core";
export function decide(broker: DurableAIExecutionBroker, request: AIExecutionRequest) { return broker.decide(request); }
```


#### `plan`

Selects a route and creates a queue record with host-controlled worker/dispatch/runner bindings.

Parameters:

- `input`: Routing and task must have matching tenantId/userId; queue metadata follows AIJobSubmission.

Returns: Decision and newly created job; caller-supplied broker route/dispatch/runner execution fields are stripped before selected bindings are written.

### Remarks

No persistence or deduplication occurs until enqueue; repeated plan calls generate different job IDs.

### Errors and rejections

Principal mismatch, unavailable route, invalid core routing, clone/hash/clock, or job creation failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableAIExecutionBroker } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
import type { AIJobSubmission } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
export function plan(broker: DurableAIExecutionBroker, input: AIJobSubmission) { return broker.plan(input); }
```


#### `enqueue`

Plans routing and atomically inserts or deduplicates the queue job in a caller-owned session.

Parameters:

- `tx`: Authorized atomic transaction/session; caller owns commit/rollback.
- `input`: Verified routing/task and queue metadata.

Returns: Decision plus the newly saved or existing idempotent job.

### Remarks

Selection still runs before deduplication; the returned existing job is authoritative for its persisted routing. No runtime execution occurs.

### Errors and rejections

Planning errors, conflicting deduplication input, corrupt index, or session failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableAIExecutionBroker } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
import type { AIJobSubmission } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
import type { AtomicSession } from "@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic";
export async function enqueue(broker: DurableAIExecutionBroker, tx: AtomicSession, input: AIJobSubmission) { return broker.enqueue(tx, input); }
```



### Example

```typescript
import { DurableAIExecutionBroker } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/ai-broker";
export function broker(options: ConstructorParameters<typeof DurableAIExecutionBroker>[0]) {
  return new DurableAIExecutionBroker(options);
}
```


<a id="api-DurableWorkflowCoordinator"></a>

## [CLASS] `DurableWorkflowCoordinator`

Keeps the business workflow instance synchronized with the LangGraph
checkpoint without making either one the other's database implementation.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-coordinator`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class DurableWorkflowCoordinator extends ServerWorkflowManager {
    constructor(options: DurableWorkflowCoordinatorOptions);
    start(graph: AgentGraphEngine, record: WorkflowInstanceRecord, initialState: AgentGraphState): Promise<AgentGraphState>;
    runWorkflow(graph: AgentGraphEngine, initialState: AgentGraphState): Promise<AgentGraphState>;
    handleApproval(graph: AgentGraphEngine, payload: ServerApprovalCallbackPayload): Promise<{
        resumed: boolean;
        state?: AgentGraphState;
        error?: string;
    }>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `DurableWorkflowCoordinatorOptions` | Yes | Host store, approval notification, and live resume authorization. |

### Returns

`DurableWorkflowCoordinator`

### Remarks

Checkpoint and companion record updates are separate operations; failures can leave them temporarily divergent. The host owns writer serialization, tenant authorization, durable stores, and reconciliation rather than blind retry after partial outcomes.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

If store is missing.

### Public members

#### `start`

Creates a queued companion instance then runs and persists its graph outcome.

Parameters:

- `graph`: Configured graph with appropriate checkpoint persistence.
- `record`: Host-admitted instance metadata; instanceId and tenantId must match initialState.
- `initialState`: Verified workflow identity and starting state.

Returns: Graph state after execution and companion CAS persistence.

### Remarks

The queued record can exist even if graph execution later fails; no cross-store rollback occurs. Atomic duplicate prevention belongs to store.create.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects alignment mismatch, existing instance, graph/callback/clone/store failures, or companion revision conflict.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableWorkflowCoordinator } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-coordinator";
import type { AgentGraphEngine, AgentGraphState } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
import type { WorkflowInstanceRecord } from "@alneas/eaos-core";
export async function start(coordinator: DurableWorkflowCoordinator, graph: AgentGraphEngine, record: WorkflowInstanceRecord, state: AgentGraphState) { return coordinator.start(graph, record, state); }
```


#### `runWorkflow`

Runs an existing graph instance and CAS-updates its companion status.

Parameters:

- `graph`: Graph whose session already has a companion record.
- `initialState`: Verified state aligned with that record.

Returns: Graph result after companion persistence; status prioritizes pending approval, error, completion, then running.

### Errors and rejections

Graph/store/clock failures, missing companion, or changed revision; graph checkpoints may already have advanced.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableWorkflowCoordinator } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-coordinator";
import type { AgentGraphEngine, AgentGraphState } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
export async function run(coordinator: DurableWorkflowCoordinator, graph: AgentGraphEngine, state: AgentGraphState) { return coordinator.runWorkflow(graph, state); }
```


#### `handleApproval`

Resumes a verified graph approval then persists its resulting companion state.

Parameters:

- `graph`: Graph owning the pending checkpoint.
- `payload`: Host-authenticated approver decision and optional binding checks.

Returns: Resume outcome; companion persistence failure becomes resumed:false error data even when graph resume already succeeded.

### Remarks

A false result does not prove no side effects occurred; reconcile graph and companion state before retrying.

### Errors and rejections

Underlying graph/store failures outside normalized resume/persistence handling may reject.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableWorkflowCoordinator } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-coordinator";
import type { AgentGraphEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph";
import type { ServerApprovalCallbackPayload } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/types";
export async function approve(coordinator: DurableWorkflowCoordinator, graph: AgentGraphEngine, payload: ServerApprovalCallbackPayload) { return coordinator.handleApproval(graph, payload); }
```


#### `handleApproval.resumed`

True only when graph resumption and companion-instance persistence complete; false may also mean companion persistence failed after the graph advanced.


#### `handleApproval.state`

Optional resumed graph state returned when companion persistence succeeds; omitted when companion persistence is normalized into failure data.


#### `handleApproval.error`

Optional graph resume or companion persistence failure detail; reconcile both stores before retrying because graph effects may already have completed.



### Example

```typescript
import { DurableWorkflowCoordinator } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-coordinator";
import type { DurableWorkflowCoordinatorOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-coordinator";
export function coordinator(options: DurableWorkflowCoordinatorOptions) { return new DurableWorkflowCoordinator(options); }
```

Trusted plugin manifests registered sequentially during initialize.

Optional host UI theme metadata retained in config; the server engine does not apply it.

Optional host UI accent color; not interpreted by this engine.

Optional host UI logo URL; not fetched by this engine.

Optional host driver metadata retained in config; this engine does not create a database connection.

#### `cors`

Optional exact browser allowOrigins list; empty/absent disables CORS middleware.

Exact allowed browser origins; credentials are enabled for configured CORS.


#### `auth`

Optional verifier and skipped path prefixes; see AuthMiddlewareOptions.


#### `auth.verifier`

Optional verified session/API-key adapter; omission installs no authentication.


#### `auth.skipPaths`

Authentication-exempt path prefixes; defaults follow createAuthMiddleware.


#### `validateSecrets`

Validate each manifest's declared secrets unless exactly false. Defaults to true.


#### `middleware`

Host composition callbacks invoked synchronously after shared authentication and before plugin route guards; each receives the app and returns no value.

<a id="api-enqueueAgentJob"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `enqueueAgentJob`

Persists a job and tenant/kind/idempotency index in the caller's atomic transaction.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/agent-jobs`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function enqueueAgentJob(tx: AtomicSession, job: AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>): Promise<AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Authorized active atomic session; the caller owns commit/rollback. |
| `job` | `AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>` | Yes | Created job whose tenant/kind/key define deduplication and whose requestHash binds input. |

### Returns

`Promise<AgentJobRecord<ServerAgentTaskRequest>>`

A clone of the saved job, or existing indexed job when its request hash matches; existing lifecycle state is preserved.

### Remarks

This helper neither executes the job nor opens a transaction; host transaction isolation/CAS must prevent concurrent index creation races.

### Errors and rejections

Reused idempotency key with a different request hash, missing indexed job, or propagated transaction/clone errors.

### Example

```typescript

import type { ServerAgentTaskRequest } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/types";
export async function enqueue(tx: AtomicSession, request: ServerAgentTaskRequest) {
  return enqueueAgentJob(tx, createAgentJob({ request, kind: "workflow" }));
}
```

<a id="api-ErpEngine"></a>

## [CLASS] `ErpEngine`

Registers plugin manifests and composes Hono routes with host authentication, entitlement, and lifecycle adapters.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/engine`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class ErpEngine {
    readonly registry: PluginRegistry;
    readonly gatekeeper: McpGatekeeper;
    constructor(config: EaosConfig);
    initialize(): Promise<void>;
    createApp(options?: CreateAppOptions): Hono<EaosEnv>;
    getRegisteredPlugins(): PluginManifest[];
    getAllMcpTools(): _alneas_eaos_core.McpToolDefinition[];
    getConfig(): EaosConfig;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config` | `EaosConfig` | Yes | App label, plugin manifests, and optional host composition settings. |

### Returns

`ErpEngine`

### Remarks

Constructing the engine creates no HTTP listener or persistent store. Initialize once before composing apps. Configuration is retained by reference. Authentication is installed only when a verifier is supplied; custom routes need their own authorization policies beyond the shared middleware.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `registry`

Public plugin registry populated during initialize; external mutation affects subsequently composed apps.


#### `gatekeeper`

Shared MCP policy registry populated from plugin manifests during initialize.


#### `initialize`

Registers manifests and gatekeeper policies and validates declared plugin secrets by default.

Returns: No value; resolves after registration and validation, or immediately after a prior successful initialization.

### Remarks

Registration occurs before secret validation, so failure can leave partial registry state. Concurrent initialization is not serialized and retrying a failed initialization may encounter already-registered IDs. Create a new engine after correcting failed setup. No migrations or plugin activation are performed.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects duplicate plugin IDs, registry failures, or secret validation failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { createErpEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/engine";
const engine = createErpEngine({ appName: "example-service", plugins: [] });
await engine.initialize();
console.log(engine.getRegisteredPlugins().length); // 0
```


#### `createApp`

Composes registered plugin routes, shared middleware, optional MCP/custom routes, and public health endpoints.

Parameters:

- `options`: Live host adapters and route settings; see [CreateAppOptions](#api-CreateAppOptions).

Returns: A new Hono app sharing this engine registry, gatekeeper, and configured adapters; it does not start a server.

### Remarks

Module guarding defaults on. Lifecycle enforcement is installed only when supplied, while declared plugin entitlements require their corresponding runtime checks. CORS uses configured origins with credentials enabled; unknown origins receive the first configured allow-origin value. Repeated calls create separate routers but may reuse host dependencies.

### Errors and rejections

Before initialization, or for synchronous middleware, plugin route factory, or health setup failures. Request-time adapter errors pass through the app error handler.

Example:

```typescript
import { createErpEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/engine";
const engine = createErpEngine({ appName: "example-service", plugins: [] });
await engine.initialize();
const app = engine.createApp();
console.log((await app.request("/health/live")).status);
```


#### `getRegisteredPlugins`

Reads the manifests currently registered in this engine.

Returns: Registry manifest list, empty before registration or with no configured plugins; objects are not deep-cloned by this method.

Example:

```typescript
import { createErpEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/engine";
const engine = createErpEngine({ appName: "example-service", plugins: [] });
await engine.initialize();
console.log(engine.getRegisteredPlugins()); // []
```


#### `getAllMcpTools`

Collects MCP tool definitions from all currently registered manifests.

Returns: Registry tool definitions, or an empty array when none exist; this list is not filtered for a request principal or tenant.

Example:

```typescript
import { createErpEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/engine";
const engine = createErpEngine({ appName: "example-service", plugins: [] });
await engine.initialize();
console.log(engine.getAllMcpTools()); // []
```


#### `getConfig`

Reads the host configuration retained at construction.

Returns: The original mutable configuration object; no cloning occurs.

Example:

```typescript
import { createErpEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/engine";
const engine = createErpEngine({ appName: "example-service", plugins: [] });
await engine.initialize();
console.log(engine.getConfig().appName);
```



### Example

```typescript
import { createErpEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-server/engine";
const engine = createErpEngine({ appName: "example-service", plugins: [] });
await engine.initialize();
const app = engine.createApp();
console.log((await app.request("/health/live")).status); // 200
```

<a id="api-EventAgentBridge"></a>

## [CLASS] `EventAgentBridge`

Converts subscribed domain events into bounded local execution or host-persisted agent work.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class EventAgentBridge {
    constructor(eventBus: DomainEventBus, worker: ServerAutonomousWorker, options?: EventAgentBridgeOptions);
    withDurableTaskStore(store: EventAgentTaskStore): this;
    runDurableOnce(limit?: number): Promise<{
        claimed: number;
        completed: number;
        failed: number;
    }>;
    registerRule(rule: EventAgentRule): () => void;
    whenIdle(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eventBus` | `DomainEventBus` | Yes | Host domain bus; subscriptions begin only on registerRule. |
| `worker` | `ServerAutonomousWorker` | Yes | Host worker performing gatekeeper/runtime execution. |
| `options` | `EventAgentBridgeOptions` | No | Queue limits, notification/error callbacks, and optional durable store. |

### Returns

`EventAgentBridge`

### Remarks

Without taskStore, accepted work is process-local and can be lost on restart. With taskStore, the host explicitly calls runDurableOnce; event subscription callbacks still do not await durable persistence from the publisher's perspective. Authorize identity in createTask before creating specifications. Generated task IDs/idempotency defaults are per emission, so repeated events are not automatically deduplicated. Dispose every registerRule callback to release subscriptions; no global destroy is provided.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

Invalid limits or malformed durable store.

### Public members

#### `withDurableTaskStore`

Persisted event work is deliberately drained by the host scheduler. The
bridge never treats its in-memory queue as a durable workflow checkpoint.

Parameters:

- `store`: Host durable queue with enqueue/claim/complete/fail functions.

Returns: This bridge after replacing its store reference.

### Remarks

Existing local queued work is not migrated by changing this store.

### Errors and rejections

Missing/malformed store functions.

Example:

```typescript
import { EventAgentBridge } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
import type { EventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
export function persist(bridge: EventAgentBridge, store: EventAgentTaskStore) { return bridge.withDurableTaskStore(store); }
```


#### `runDurableOnce`

Claims one bounded durable batch and processes it sequentially.

Parameters:

- `limit`: Safe integer 1–maxConcurrent; defaults to maxConcurrent.

Returns: Claim/completion/failure persistence counts; a worker FAILED result counts completed if stored successfully.

### Remarks

Calls are not globally serialized. Notification failures are reported after result persistence. No periodic scheduler or automatic retry is installed.

### Errors and rejections

Missing store, invalid limit, claim/fail persistence errors, or synchronous error-sink errors.

Example:

```typescript
import { EventAgentBridge } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
export async function drain(bridge: EventAgentBridge) { return bridge.runDurableOnce(); }
```


#### `runDurableOnce.claimed`

Number of queued tasks returned by the host claim for this pass, including tasks later recorded as completed or failed.


#### `runDurableOnce.completed`

Number of task results successfully passed to store.complete; a returned worker FAILED or PENDING_APPROVAL status still counts when its result is stored.


#### `runDurableOnce.failed`

Number of worker throws or store.complete failures handled through store.fail; this counts persistence/execution handling failures rather than every returned worker FAILED status.


#### `registerRule`

Subscribes a task-conversion rule and returns its individual unsubscribe callback.

Parameters:

- `rule`: Exact event name and synchronous createTask callback; callback receives payload and returns verified task fields or null to skip.

Returns: A no-argument callback returning no value; removes this rule and unsubscribes the bus handler when no rules remain.

### Remarks

The rule is retained by reference; do not mutate its eventName after registration. Already accepted tasks keep running after unsubscribe.

### Errors and rejections

Event bus subscription/unsubscription errors can propagate. Event conversion errors are reported through onError.

Example:

```typescript
import { EventAgentBridge } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
import type { EventAgentRule } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
export function listen(bridge: EventAgentBridge, rule: EventAgentRule) { return bridge.registerRule(rule); }
```


#### `whenIdle`

Waits until the bridge's local active count and waiting queue are empty.

Returns: No value; resolves when local work is idle. It does not wait for durable queue persistence/draining or asynchronous error sinks.

### Remarks

Polls with zero-delay timers and has no timeout/cancellation; continuously arriving work can delay completion indefinitely.

Example:

```typescript
import { EventAgentBridge } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
export async function idle(bridge: EventAgentBridge) { await bridge.whenIdle(); }
```



### Example

```typescript
import { EventAgentBridge } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
import type { DomainEventBus } from "@alneas/eaos-core";
import type { ServerAutonomousWorker } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/autonomous-worker";
export function bridge(eventBus: DomainEventBus, worker: ServerAutonomousWorker) { return new EventAgentBridge(eventBus, worker); }
```

<a id="api-EventAgentTaskStore"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `EventAgentTaskStore`

Host-owned durable queue for event-triggered agent work.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface EventAgentTaskStore {
    enqueue(task: QueuedEventTask): Promise<void>;
    claim(limit: number): Promise<readonly QueuedEventTask[]>;
    complete(taskId: string, result: ServerAgentTaskResult): Promise<void>;
    fail(taskId: string, error: unknown): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enqueue` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Persists accepted event work before a scheduler drains it. |
| `claim` | `Promise<readonly QueuedEventTask[]>` | Yes | Exclusively claims work for one drain pass. |
| `complete` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Persists the normalized result for a claimed task. |
| `fail` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Records or handles a claimed execution/persistence failure. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

EventAgentBridge.withDurableTaskStore for usage.

### Public members

#### `enqueue`

Persists accepted event work before a scheduler drains it.

Parameters:

- `task`: Verified generated task and cloneable event payload.

Returns: No value; resolves after host persistence.

### Errors and rejections

Queue failures propagate to bridge error reporting.

Example:

```typescript
import type { EventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function enqueueAdmittedEventTask(
  store: EventAgentTaskStore, task: Parameters<EventAgentTaskStore["enqueue"]>[0],
) {
  // Host admission and the event-to-task mapping run before queue insertion.
  await store.enqueue(task);
}
```


#### `claim`

Exclusively claims work for one drain pass.

Parameters:

- `limit`: Requested maximum item count.

Returns: Claimed queue items, or an empty array.

### Errors and rejections

Queue failures reject the drain pass.

Example:

```typescript
import type { EventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function claimEventTasks(store: EventAgentTaskStore) {
  const tasks = await store.claim(10);
  return tasks; // Empty when no eligible tasks are available.
}
```


#### `complete`

Persists the normalized result for a claimed task.

Parameters:

- `taskId`: Claimed task identifier.
- `result`: Runtime outcome, including failed/pending statuses.

Returns: No value; resolves after persistence.

### Errors and rejections

Completion failure causes the bridge to call fail.

Example:

```typescript
import type { EventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function completeEventTask(
  store: EventAgentTaskStore, claimedTaskId: string,
  result: Parameters<EventAgentTaskStore["complete"]>[1],
) {
  await store.complete(claimedTaskId, result);
  // The host decides persistence and result retention for this queue.
}
```


#### `fail`

Records or handles a claimed execution/persistence failure.

Parameters:

- `taskId`: Claimed task identifier.
- `error`: Underlying execution or completion failure.

Returns: No value; completion/retry semantics belong to the host store.

### Errors and rejections

Failures reject the drain pass.

Example:

```typescript
import type { EventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function recordEventTaskFailure(
  store: EventAgentTaskStore, claimedTaskId: string, observedError: unknown,
) {
  await store.fail(claimedTaskId, observedError);
  // Failure/retry policy belongs to the host store; this does not retry execution.
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-FileLifecycleStore"></a>

## [CLASS] `FileLifecycleStore`

Single control-plane filesystem. All backend processes must read the same ledger.
A crashed writer leaves its lock in place: reconcile DB/infra before operator recovery.
For independent hosts, implement LifecycleStore using a shared transactional control DB.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class FileLifecycleStore implements LifecycleStore {
    readonly path: string;
    constructor(path: string);
    read(): Promise<LifecycleState>;
    withLock<T>(fn: (writer: LifecycleWriter) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | Yes | Ledger filename, resolved relative to the current process directory. |

### Returns

`FileLifecycleStore`

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `path`

Absolute ledger path resolved at construction; lock directory is path + ".lock".


#### `read`

Reads and normalizes the JSON lifecycle ledger.

Returns: Stored lifecycle state, or a fresh empty state if the file does not exist.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects filesystem, JSON parsing, or state-normalization failures other than ENOENT.

Example:

```typescript
import { FileLifecycleStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle";
const state = await new FileLifecycleStore("./state/lifecycle.json").read();
console.log(state.platform);
```


#### `withLock`

Runs one writer callback under an exclusive filesystem lock directory.

Parameters:

- `fn`: Called after lock acquisition with ledger read and durable write operations; must await its writes before returning.

Returns: The callback result after lock directory removal. Writer.write resolves without a value after temporary-file fsync, rename, and directory fsync.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Callback result passed through unchanged.

### Remarks

Lock acquisition does not wait or retry. Ordinary callback failure removes the lock; a process crash can leave it behind and requires operator reconciliation. Writes may have committed before a later failure. The store does not enforce that all external writers use this lock.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects an existing lock, filesystem failures, callback failures, or final lock-removal failures.

Example:

```typescript
import { FileLifecycleStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle";
const store = new FileLifecycleStore("./state/lifecycle.json");
const state = await store.withLock(async writer => writer.read());
console.log(state.platform);
```



### Example

```typescript
import { FileLifecycleStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle";

console.log((await store.read()).platform);
```

```

<a id="api-GraphProjectionCoordinator"></a>

## [CLASS] `GraphProjectionCoordinator`

Applies domain events to an ADB Graph/PGQL or other relationship read model.

The coordinator is intentionally independent of Oracle. The host supplies
the adapter and cursor store, so credentials, graph schema and transaction
policy never enter core/server.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph-projection`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class GraphProjectionCoordinator {
    constructor(options: GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions);
    apply(event: Readonly<WorkflowEventEnvelope>): Promise<void>;
    rebuild(tenantId: string, sourceRevision: number, snapshot: unknown): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions` | Yes | Host projection dependencies. |

### Returns

`GraphProjectionCoordinator`

### Remarks

Calls are not serialized by this class. The host must coordinate writers/rebuilds, authorize tenant data, and make adapter replay safe. Adapter changes and cursor writes are separate operations; a cursor failure can leave projection data applied but unacknowledged.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

If projectionId is blank or adapter/cursorStore is absent.

### Public members

#### `apply`

Applies one event and records projection progress, skipping recognized duplicate/stale events.

Parameters:

- `event`: Trusted workflow event envelope; the adapter receives a structured clone.

Returns: No value; resolves after application and cursor persistence or immediately for the last event ID or a nonincreasing revision of the last aggregate.

### Remarks

A revision gap for the last aggregate increments lagCount and records lagging but still applies the event. Deduplication covers only the last event/aggregate cursor, not full history. Failure may occur after adapter side effects; no rollback or retry occurs here.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects rebuilding state, cursor/clock/clone failures, or adapter failures. Adapter failure attempts a failed cursor write, which can itself replace the original error.

Example:

```typescript
import { GraphProjectionCoordinator, type GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph-projection";
import type { WorkflowEventEnvelope } from "@alneas/eaos-core";
export async function apply(options: GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions, event: WorkflowEventEnvelope) {
  await new GraphProjectionCoordinator(options).apply(event);
}
```


#### `rebuild`

Marks a tenant projection rebuilding, delegates snapshot replacement, then records healthy or failed state.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Verified tenant whose relationship model is rebuilt.
- `sourceRevision`: Host source revision copied to the rebuilt cursor; not validated by this coordinator.
- `snapshot`: Host-authorized snapshot cloned before passing to the adapter.

Returns: No value; resolves after adapter rebuild and healthy cursor persistence.

### Remarks

No cancellation or exclusive lock is acquired. The host must serialize rebuild/application and determine recovery after partial adapter or cursor failure.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects clock, cursor, clone, or adapter failures; a failed-status write can replace an earlier failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { GraphProjectionCoordinator, type GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph-projection";
export async function rebuild(options: GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions, tenantId: string, revision: number, snapshot: unknown) {
  await new GraphProjectionCoordinator(options).rebuild(tenantId, revision, snapshot);
}
```



### Example

```typescript
import { GraphProjectionCoordinator, type GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph-projection";
export function projection(options: GraphProjectionCoordinatorOptions) {
  return new GraphProjectionCoordinator(options);
}
```

## [INTERFACE] `GraphSubgraph`

Minimal boundary for a compiled LangGraph subgraph. The plugin owns its state schema.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/graph`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface GraphSubgraph {
    invoke(input: unknown, config?: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
    getState?(config?: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
    resume?(input: unknown, decision: GraphApprovalDecision, config?: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke` | `Promise<unknown>` | Yes | Invokes the compiled child graph. |
| `getState` | `Promise<unknown>` | No | Inspects child state when a recognized interrupt needs mapping. |
| `resume` | `Promise<unknown>` | No | Continues a child after a verified parent approval. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

AgentGraphEngine.addSubgraph for setup and usage.

### Public members

#### `invoke`

Invokes the compiled child graph.

Parameters:

- `input`: Host-mapped child input.
- `config`: Parent-supplied checkpoint thread/namespace configuration.

Returns: Child output, interpreted by the parent mapOutput callback.

### Errors and rejections

Child execution/checkpoint failures propagate or can be mapped for recognized interrupts.

Example:

```typescript
import type { GraphSubgraph } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
export async function invokeHostSubgraph(
  subgraph: GraphSubgraph,
  input: Parameters<GraphSubgraph["invoke"]>[0],
  config: Parameters<GraphSubgraph["invoke"]>[1],
) {
  // Supply the host's admitted input and checkpoint/thread configuration.
  return await subgraph.invoke(input, config);
}
```


#### `getState`

Inspects child state when a recognized interrupt needs mapping.

Parameters:

- `config`: Child checkpoint thread/namespace configuration.

Returns: Host-specific child checkpoint state.

### Errors and rejections

Inspection failures propagate to parent execution.

Example:

```typescript
* ```typescript
 import type { GraphSubgraph } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
 export async function inspectHostSubgraph(
 subgraph: GraphSubgraph, config: Parameters<NonNullable<GraphSubgraph["getState"]>>[0],
 ) {
 if (!subgraph.getState) throw new Error("Subgraph state inspection is unavailable");
 return await subgraph.getState(config);
 }
 ```
```


#### `resume`

Continues a child after a verified parent approval.

Parameters:

- `input`: Host-mapped child input.
- `decision`: Parent-approved human decision.
- `config`: Child checkpoint thread/namespace configuration.

Returns: Resumed child output.

### Errors and rejections

Child execution/checkpoint failures propagate.

Example:

```typescript
* ```typescript
 import type { GraphSubgraph } from "@alneas/eaos-server";
 export async function resumeHostSubgraph(
 subgraph: GraphSubgraph,
 input: Parameters<NonNullable<GraphSubgraph["resume"]>>[0],
 verifiedDecision: Parameters<NonNullable<GraphSubgraph["resume"]>>[1],
 config: Parameters<NonNullable<GraphSubgraph["resume"]>>[2],
 ) {
 if (!subgraph.resume) throw new Error("Subgraph resumption is unavailable");
 // The host authenticates/authorizes this decision before entering the subgraph.
 return await subgraph.resume(input, verifiedDecision, config);
 }
 ```
```

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `status` | `'COMPLETED' \| 'FAILED'` | Yes | COMPLETED requires string output; FAILED is converted to a rejected execution. |
| `output` | `string` | No | Required string result for COMPLETED replies; ignored on FAILED. |
| `error` | `string` | No | Optional failure description; a blank/missing value uses a generic message. |
| `failureCode` | `WorkflowAgentFailureCode` | No | Optional recognized classification; unrecognized values become RUNTIME_FAILED. |
| `retryable` | `boolean` | No | Optional retry advice on failures; otherwise unavailable/timeout/runtime failure default to retryable. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Public members

#### `protocolVersion`

Wire protocol version; must match 1.0.


#### `taskId`

Must match the submitted task ID.


#### `status`

COMPLETED requires string output; FAILED is converted to a rejected execution.


#### `output`

Required string result for COMPLETED replies; ignored on FAILED.


#### `error`

Optional failure description; a blank/missing value uses a generic message.


#### `failureCode`

Optional recognized classification; unrecognized values become RUNTIME_FAILED.


#### `retryable`

Optional retry advice on failures; otherwise unavailable/timeout/runtime failure default to retryable.

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-inheritAtomicSqlSession"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `inheritAtomicSqlSession`

Temporarily propagate an existing joined SQL capability to a validated session wrapper.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic-context`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function inheritAtomicSqlSession(source: AtomicSession, wrapper: AtomicSession): () => void;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Currently bound source session; if unbound no capability is created. |
| `wrapper` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Wrapper session whose lifetime must not exceed the parent callback. |

### Returns

`() => void`

A release callback deleting the wrapper's propagated binding.

### Remarks

Internal trusted capability plumbing exposed for validated host adapters. It never opens a transaction, authenticates a principal or extends the underlying session lifetime.

### Example

```typescript
import { inheritAtomicSqlSession } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic-context'
export function withBinding(source: Parameters<typeof inheritAtomicSqlSession>[0], wrapper: Parameters<typeof inheritAtomicSqlSession>[1], work: () => void) { const release = inheritAtomicSqlSession(source, wrapper); try { work() } finally { release() } }
```

<a id="api-InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore"></a>

## [CLASS] `InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore`

Small process-local TaskStore for development, tests and a single short-
lived host. It deliberately has no lease recovery or persistence and must
not be used as the production workflow/checkpoint store.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore implements EventAgentTaskStore {
    constructor(options?: {
        maxTasks?: number;
    });
    enqueue(task: QueuedEventTask): Promise<void>;
    claim(limit: number): Promise<readonly QueuedEventTask[]>;
    complete(taskId: string, result: ServerAgentTaskResult): Promise<void>;
    fail(taskId: string, _error: unknown): Promise<void>;
    getResult(taskId: string): ServerAgentTaskResult | undefined;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     maxTasks?: number; }` | No | maxTasks defaults to 10000 and must be a safe integer 1–1000000. |

### Returns

`InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore`

### Remarks

Duplicate IDs compare JSON serialization exactly. Completed history/results are retained without the active-task capacity limit. No retry, lease recovery, or durable failure history exists.

### Constructor contract

### Errors and rejections

Invalid capacity.

### Public members

#### `constructor.options.maxTasks`

Maximum pending plus claimed tasks retained at once; defaults to 10000 and must be a safe integer from 1 to 1000000. Completed history/results are outside this limit.


#### `enqueue`

Clones a queued task unless its ID is already identically retained.

Parameters:

- `task`: Nonempty task ID and event name with structured-cloneable payload/task.

Returns: No value; resolves after local insertion or matching duplicate detection.

### Errors and rejections

Missing identifiers, conflicting duplicate, active capacity exhaustion, or clone/JSON failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
import type { QueuedEventTask } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
export async function enqueue(store: InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore, task: QueuedEventTask) { await store.enqueue(task); }
```


#### `claim`

Moves pending items into the claimed map in insertion order.

Parameters:

- `limit`: Positive safe-integer maximum item count.

Returns: Cloned claimed items, or an empty array.

### Errors and rejections

Invalid limit or clone failure; an item may already have moved before clone failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
const store = new InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore();
console.log(await store.claim(1)); // []
```


#### `complete`

Moves a claimed task into retained completion history and clones its result.

Parameters:

- `taskId`: Current claimed task identifier.
- `result`: Normalized runtime outcome, including FAILED or PENDING_APPROVAL data.

Returns: No value; completes after retaining history and result.

### Errors and rejections

Unknown/already completed task or clone failure; history can already have changed.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
import type { ServerAgentTaskResult } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/types";
export async function complete(store: InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore, taskId: string, result: ServerAgentTaskResult) { await store.complete(taskId, result); }
```


#### `fail`

Removes a claimed task without retaining failure history or rescheduling it.

Parameters:

- `taskId`: Current claimed task identifier.
- `_error`: Failure value accepted for interface compatibility and ignored.

Returns: No value; resolves after removal.

### Errors and rejections

Unknown/already failed task.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
export async function fail(store: InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore, taskId: string, error: unknown) { await store.fail(taskId, error); }
```


#### `getResult`

Inspects a cloned retained completion result for local tests/development.

Parameters:

- `taskId`: Previously completed task identifier.

Returns: Cloned result, or undefined if no completion result exists.

### Errors and rejections

If a retained result cannot be cloned.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
console.log(new InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore().getResult("missing")); // undefined
```



### Example

```typescript
import { InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/event-bridge";
const store = new InMemoryEventAgentTaskStore();
console.log(await store.claim(1)); // []
```


<a id="api-InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry"></a>

## [CLASS] `InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry`

Stores versioned workflow drafts and validated/approved/published/retired records in process memory.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry implements WorkflowDefinitionRegistry {
    constructor(options?: {
        now?: () => string;
        validate?: (definition: WorkflowDefinition) => void;
    });
    saveDraft(input: unknown, actorId?: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord;
    validate(workflowId: string, version: string, actorId?: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord;
    approve(workflowId: string, version: string, actorId: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord;
    publish(workflowId: string, version: string, actorId: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord;
    retire(workflowId: string, version: string, actorId: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord;
    get(workflowId: string, version: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord | undefined;
    getPublished(workflowId: string): WorkflowDefinitionRecord | undefined;
    list(workflowId?: string): readonly WorkflowDefinitionRecord[];
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     now?: () => string;     validate?: (definition: WorkflowDefinition) => void; }` | No | now returns a timestamp string and defaults to current ISO time; validate synchronously checks a structurally valid draft during validate and may throw. |

### Returns

`InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry`

### Remarks

Reference registry for tests/local authoring; it performs no actor authentication, role authorization, durable storage, or cross-process coordination. Transitions increment record revision and preserve definitions after draft.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `constructor.options.now`

Optional timestamp-string clock used when creating/updating registry records; defaults to current ISO time.

Returns: Timestamp text recorded without additional format validation by this registry.

### See also

[InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry.saveDraft](#api-InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry)


#### `constructor.options.validate`

Optional synchronous host semantic validator called after Core structural validation during a draft-to-validated transition.

Parameters:

- `definition`: Structurally valid stored workflow definition presented for host semantic checks.

Returns: No value when accepted; throw to reject validation before the status update.

### Remarks

The callback receives the stored definition reference, so it should inspect without mutating it; this registry supplies no actor authentication or cross-process coordination.

### See also

[InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry.validate](#api-InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry)


#### `saveDraft`

Validates and inserts or replaces a draft version, incrementing its revision.

Parameters:

- `input`: Unknown workflow definition validated by core validation.
- `actorId`: Optional author label recorded as creator/updater; not authenticated here.

Returns: A cloned draft record with canonical definition hash.

### Errors and rejections

Invalid definition, non-draft existing version, clock/hash/clone failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
export function draft(input: unknown) { return new InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry().saveDraft(input); }
```


#### `validate`

Transitions an existing draft to validated after core and optional host checks.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier.
- `version`: Exact stored version.
- `actorId`: Optional updater label.

Returns: A cloned validated record with incremented revision.

### Errors and rejections

Missing version, nondraft status, validation/callback/clock failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
export function validate(registry: InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry, workflowId: string, version: string) { return registry.validate(workflowId, version); }
```


#### `approve`

Transitions a validated version to approved and records approver metadata.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier.
- `version`: Exact stored version.
- `actorId`: Nonblank verified host approver label; no role check occurs here.

Returns: A cloned approved record.

### Errors and rejections

Blank actor, missing version, nonvalidated status, or clock failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
export function approve(registry: InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry, workflowId: string, version: string, actorId: string) { return registry.approve(workflowId, version, actorId); }
```


#### `publish`

Publishes an approved version and retires any currently published version of the same workflow.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier.
- `version`: Approved version to publish.
- `actorId`: Nonblank verified host publisher label.

Returns: A cloned published record; previous published records become retired.

### Errors and rejections

Blank actor, missing version, nonapproved status, or clock/clone failure; earlier retirement updates can already have occurred.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
export function publish(registry: InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry, workflowId: string, version: string, actorId: string) { return registry.publish(workflowId, version, actorId); }
```


#### `retire`

Transitions a published version to retired and records retirement metadata.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier.
- `version`: Currently published version.
- `actorId`: Nonblank verified host operator label.

Returns: A cloned retired record.

### Errors and rejections

Blank actor, missing version, nonpublished status, or clock failure.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
export function retire(registry: InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry, workflowId: string, version: string, actorId: string) { return registry.retire(workflowId, version, actorId); }
```


#### `get`

Reads one workflow version without mutating lifecycle state.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier.
- `version`: Exact stored version.

Returns: A cloned record, or undefined when absent.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
console.log(new InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry().get("example", "1.0.0")); // undefined
```


#### `getPublished`

Finds the currently published version of one workflow.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier.

Returns: A cloned published record, or undefined when none exists.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
console.log(new InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry().getPublished("example")); // undefined
```


#### `list`

Lists records in insertion order with optional workflow filtering.

Parameters:

- `workflowId`: Exact workflow identifier to filter, or omit for all workflows.

Returns: Independent cloned records, or an empty array.

Example:

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
console.log(new InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry().list()); // []
```



### Example

```typescript
import { InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry } from "@alneas/eaos-server/agentic/workflow-registry";
const registry = new InMemoryWorkflowDefinitionRegistry();
console.log(registry.list()); // []
```

<a id="api-isNoCacheRequested"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `isNoCacheRequested`

Detects request directives or query flags asking to bypass cached values.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/cache`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function isNoCacheRequested(c: Pick<Context, 'req'>): boolean;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `c` | `Pick<Context, 'req'>` | Yes | Hono request context; reads Cache-Control, Pragma, refresh, and nocache. |

### Returns

`boolean`

True for no-cache, max-age=0 (optionally quoted), or refresh/nocache equal to true or 1; false otherwise. Header directives are case-insensitive; query flag values are case-sensitive.

### Example

```typescript
import { Hono } from "hono";
import { isNoCacheRequested } from "@alneas/eaos-server/cache";
const app = new Hono();
app.get("/cache-policy", c => c.json({ bypass: isNoCacheRequested(c) }));
console.log(await (await app.request("/cache-policy?refresh=1")).json());
```


<a id="api-joinedAtomicSqlExecutor"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `joinedAtomicSqlExecutor`

Expose SQL execution on the exact active transaction that owns envelope CAS and receipts.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data`, `@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data/atomic`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function joinedAtomicSqlExecutor(session: AtomicSession, principal: PluginPrincipal): {
    dialect: "sqlite" | "oracle" | "postgres";
    execute(tenantId: string, sql: string, binds: unknown[]): Promise<{
        rows?: Record<string, unknown>[];
        affectedRows: number;
    }>;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | `AtomicSession` | Yes | Currently active repository session carrying a trusted SQL capability binding. |
| `principal` | `PluginPrincipal` | Yes | Verified principal matching both tenant and user of the joined transaction. |

### Returns

`{     dialect: "sqlite" \| "oracle" \| "postgres";     execute(tenantId: string, sql: string, binds: unknown[]): Promise<{         rows?: Record<string, unknown>[];         affectedRows: number;     }>; }`

The bound driver dialect and an execute(tenantId, sql, binds) method using the existing connection.

### Remarks

Never retain or use the executor after the parent transaction callback returns. It does not open another transaction or authorize arbitrary SQL.

### Errors and rejections

Throws for malformed/mismatched principals, missing/expired transaction bindings or a foreign execute tenant; driver failures propagate.

### Example

```typescript
import { joinedAtomicSqlExecutor, type AtomicRepository, type PluginPrincipal } from '@alneas/eaos-server/plugin-data'
export function queryJoined(repository: AtomicRepository, principal: PluginPrincipal, statement: string, binds: unknown[]) {
 // The host supplies trusted SQL and verifies resource permission before entry.
 return repository.run(principal, session => joinedAtomicSqlExecutor(session, principal).execute(principal.tenantId, statement, binds))
}
```

<a id="api-LifecyclePlan"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `LifecyclePlan`

Reviewable hash-bound lifecycle transition generated against one ledger revision.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-server/lifecycle-engine`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface LifecyclePlan {
    format: 1;
    id: string;
    revision: number;
    frameworkVersion: string;
    request: LifecycleRequest;
    backend: BackendTarget;
    dataCatalog?: DataContractCatalog;
    plugins: LifecyclePlugin[];
    migrations: MigrationStep[];
    infrastructure: InfrastructureStep[];
    deactivate: string[];
    infrastructureProvider: string | null;
    retainData: true;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `1` | Yes | Plan discriminator; currently 1. |
| `id` | `string` | Yes | Canonical SHA-256 hash of all plan body fields. |
| `revision` | `number` | Yes | Ledger revision observed during planning; apply rejects stale plans. |
| `frameworkVersion` | `string` | Yes | Framework compatibility version used to resolve the plan. |
| `request` | `LifecycleRequest` | Yes | Original scoped operation request. |
| `backend` | `BackendTarget` | Yes | Snapshot of the exact immutable backend identity. |
| `dataCatalog` | `DataContractCatalog` | No | Optional dependency-resolved canonical data contracts and table ownership. |
| `plugins` | `LifecyclePlugin[]` | Yes | Dependency-ordered trusted feature releases involved in the transition. |
| `migrations` | `MigrationStep[]` | Yes | Ordered migration steps not already applied with matching checksums. |
| `infrastructure` | `InfrastructureStep[]` | Yes | Planned host infrastructure changes requiring the configured executor. |
| `deactivate` | `string[]` | Yes | Activation map keys disabled before disruptive changes. |
| `infrastructureProvider` | `string \| null` | Yes | Configured executor identity, or null when none exists. |
| `retainData` | `true` | Yes | Always true; lifecycle uninstall never drops business data. |
